item.title: Department of Commerce lifts export controls on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, access restoration to begin July 1 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: The U.S. Department of Commerce has lifted export controls on Anthropic's AI models Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5, allowing the company to begin restoring access starting July 1. Anthropic announced the development on Twitter, expressing gratitude to users for their patience and to those who assisted in redeploying the models. This decision follows a period during which access to these models was restricted due to export regulations. The restoration marks a significant step for Anthropic in resuming broader availability of its AI technologies.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5, an agentic AI model with improved reasoning, tool use, and safety, available across all plans with introductory pricing through August 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Sonnet 5, an advanced agentic AI model designed to improve reasoning, tool use, and safety. This model can autonomously plan and execute tasks using tools like browsers and terminals, offering performance close to larger, more expensive models but at a lower cost. Claude Sonnet 5 is now available across all subscription plans, including Free and Pro, with introductory pricing available through August 2026. The new model shows significant improvements over its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6, particularly in coding, knowledge work, and agentic capabilities. Safety assessments indicate a lower rate of undesirable behaviors, and it has limited ability to perform cybersecurity tasks compared to Opus models. Early users have praised its ability to complete complex, multi-step tasks efficiently and safely, making it suitable for a range of applications from software engineering to legal research and insurance workflows. Claude Sonnet 5 is accessible via the Claude API and is positioned as a cost-effective option for developers seeking powerful, autonomous AI assistance. Its release marks a notable step forward in agentic AI technology, balancing enhanced functionality with improved safety and affordability.

item.title: Researchers find Claude AI is steganographically marking user requests in prompts
item.description: Researchers have discovered that Claude AI embeds steganographic markers within user prompts, effectively encoding hidden information in the input data. This finding reveals that the AI system may be tracking or tagging user requests in a subtle, concealed manner. The discovery raises questions about privacy and transparency in AI interactions, highlighting the need for further investigation into how AI models handle and potentially encode user data.

item.title: Claude launches Claude Science, an AI-powered research platform for reproducible scientific analysis and manuscript drafting, available on macOS and Linux [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Claude has launched Claude Science, an AI-powered research platform designed to support rigorous scientific analysis and manuscript drafting. Available on macOS and Linux, the platform enables researchers to run analyses, search databases, and trace every step from data processing to publication, ensuring full reproducibility and transparency. The app features native visualization tools for proteins, molecules, and genomic data, along with built-in fact-checking to flag inconsistencies. It supports domain-specific workflows across life sciences, including genomics, proteomics, and cheminformatics, and manages computing resources from local machines to high-performance clusters. Claude Science also integrates manuscript drafting with analysis, allowing researchers to write and revise results alongside their data in a single environment. By connecting to over 60 scientific databases and offering reusable pipelines, Claude Science aims to streamline complex research projects and enhance collaboration. Early users have praised its ability to facilitate reproducible research and accelerate discovery, highlighting its potential to transform scientific workflows.

item.title: DeepMind releases Gemini Image Flash Lite model with dramatically reduced latency for faster workflows
item.description: DeepMind has introduced the Gemini Image Flash Lite model, designed to significantly reduce latency and accelerate image processing workflows. This advancement aims to enable users to explore and iterate more quickly, enhancing productivity in tasks that require rapid image analysis. The model's focus on lightning-fast latency addresses the need for efficient performance in real-time applications, allowing workflows to maintain momentum without delays. This development reflects DeepMind's ongoing efforts to optimize AI models for practical, high-speed use cases.

item.title: Meta AI releases Brain2Qwerty v2, a non-invasive AI system decoding brain waves into text with up to 78% word accuracy in real time [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Meta AI has introduced Brain2Qwerty v2, an advanced non-invasive AI system that decodes brain waves into text with up to 78% word accuracy in real time. This technology builds on the previous version by using end-to-end deep learning to interpret raw brain signals recorded via magnetoencephalography (MEG), enabling coherent sentence reconstruction without surgical implants. The system was trained on data from nine volunteers who typed while wearing MEG devices, allowing the AI to leverage semantic context through fine-tuned large language models. Brain2Qwerty v2 significantly outperforms other non-invasive methods, achieving a 61% average word accuracy and demonstrating potential to narrow the gap with invasive brain decoding techniques through further data scaling. Meta AI has released the full training code and datasets to encourage open research and collaboration, aiming to accelerate neuroscience breakthroughs and improve communication options for individuals with brain lesions. This effort is part of a broader initiative to develop foundational brain models and stimulate open datasets within the Digital Brain Project.

item.title: Mistral releases Leanstral 1.5, a 119B-parameter formal proof engineering model optimized for automated theorem proving and autoformalization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Mistral has released Leanstral 1.5, a formal proof engineering model designed to enhance automated theorem proving and autoformalization. The model features 119 billion parameters, with 6.5 billion active, and is based on the Lean 4 formal proof system. This update aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of formal proof tasks, supporting advancements in automated reasoning and formal verification processes. Leanstral 1.5 is part of Mistral's broader suite of models, which also includes Mistral Medium 3.5 and Voxtral TTS.

item.title: arXiv to spin out from Cornell University and become an independent nonprofit organization on July 1, 2026, maintaining free access and community support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: On July 1, 2026, arXiv will become an independent nonprofit organization, separating from Cornell University after 25 years. Despite this change, arXiv will continue to provide free access to scientific papers and maintain its commitment to supporting the global scientific community. The transition aims to offer greater flexibility and growth opportunities while ensuring uninterrupted service for authors and readers. The decision to spin out has been carefully planned, with staff and volunteers working to ensure a smooth transition. arXiv will uphold its mission, vision, and values, remaining a community-driven platform. To keep users informed, arXiv has launched a dedicated FAQ page and will release a series of blog posts detailing leadership updates, milestones, and policy changes, emphasizing transparency throughout the process.

item.title: Researchers study LearnStop, a learned stopping rule for reasoning models, finding its effectiveness depends on task type and is most beneficial when scalar confidence or convergence signals are unreliable [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated LearnStop, a learned stopping rule designed to optimize computation in reasoning language models by predicting when to halt processing based on multiple online features. Their study across 18 task-model settings revealed that the effectiveness of LearnStop varies by task type, showing significant improvements in free-form math problems but less advantage in multiple-choice or very challenging tasks where simpler scalar confidence or entropy measures perform comparably or better. The findings suggest that learned stopping is most beneficial when no single reliable scalar stopping signal exists, but its advantages diminish when confidence or answer convergence already provide clear stopping cues. The study evaluated LearnStop's performance using various metrics and conditions, including validation-selected operating points, risk calibration, and robustness checks, across diverse datasets such as GSM8K, MATH-500, and MMLU-Pro. The researchers emphasize that learned stopping should be viewed as a complementary tool rather than a universal replacement for scalar exit strategies, with its value depending on the structure of the reasoning process and the nature of the task.

item.title: New ARC-AGI-2 solver uses modality-driven search and holistic trace judging to achieve 72.9% accuracy on ARC Prize semi-private set, outperforming GPT-5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro by over 18 points [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new solver for the ARC-AGI-2 visual reasoning benchmark achieves a 72.9% accuracy on the ARC Prize semi-private evaluation set, outperforming leading models like GPT-5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro by over 18 percentage points. The solver uses a modality-driven search approach that generates diverse candidate solutions across text, image, and code channels, combined with a holistic judging method that evaluates all candidate reasoning traces together to select the best answer. This method effectively recovers correct minority hypotheses where majority voting fails. The solver also attains 76.1% accuracy on the public evaluation set at a lower cost per task. The developer has released the full source code and reported that certain techniques, such as prescriptive prompting and iterative refinement, reduce hypothesis diversity and negatively impact performance. This advancement highlights the importance of diverse candidate generation and comprehensive evaluation in improving abstract reasoning tasks with large language models.

item.title: Researchers present MetaFlow, a meta-learning approach to train large language models as zero-shot workflow generators with strong generalization across tasks and operator sets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MetaFlow, a meta-learning approach designed to train large language models (LLMs) as zero-shot workflow generators that generalize effectively across various tasks and operator sets. MetaFlow addresses the challenge of creating consistent, reusable workflows by learning to compose solution strategies from task and operator inputs, improving reliability and interpretability compared to instance-specific solutions. The model is trained through supervised fine-tuning on synthetic data followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, enabling it to produce effective workflows for both trained and novel tasks. MetaFlow was evaluated on benchmarks including question answering, code generation, and mathematical reasoning, where it matched state-of-the-art performance on in-domain tasks and demonstrated strong zero-shot generalization to out-of-domain tasks and new operator sets. This approach offers a scalable alternative to manual workflow design, potentially enhancing the deployment and robustness of LLM-based solutions across diverse applications.

item.title: Researchers propose ComplianceGate, a classifier-gated multi-tier routing system for large language models that enforces data residency and reduces latency and costs in regulated industries [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ComplianceGate, a classifier-gated multi-tier routing system designed for large language models (LLMs) used in regulated industries. This system addresses compliance and cost efficiency by using a trained encoder classifier to evaluate each query's complexity and data sensitivity before any model inference. Queries containing personally identifiable information (PII) are routed to local endpoints, ensuring data residency compliance, while simpler queries are directed to smaller, faster models, reducing resource use and costs. Testing on 600 queries showed that ComplianceGate reduces median latency by 39%, cuts costs by 33-52% depending on query distribution, and improves generation throughput significantly compared to baseline models. The encoder classifier achieves 99.2% accuracy with near-perfect recall for PII, operating with minimal inference overhead, demonstrating a practical approach to compliance-by-design in LLM deployment.

item.title: Researchers introduce MoralAltDataset to evaluate 15 LLMs on generating and preferring moral alternatives beyond binary dilemmas, finding LLM-generated options often surpass human ones in ethical and structural quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced MoralAltDataset, a collection of 307 moral dilemmas enhanced with compromise and reframed alternatives, to evaluate how large language models (LLMs) handle moral decision-making beyond binary choices. Testing 15 LLMs, the study found that these models often prefer compromise alternatives over original options, significantly influencing moral judgments. The research also compared LLM-generated alternatives to human-authored ones, revealing that LLMs frequently produce options that better meet detailed ethical and structural standards. The dataset includes both narrative Advisor dilemmas and AI-facing Agent dilemmas, reflecting diverse moral scenarios. Evaluations involved pairwise preference tests and expert assessments, highlighting trade-offs between the structural quality of alternatives and their practical feasibility. This work underscores the potential of LLMs to generate nuanced moral options that extend beyond traditional binary frameworks, offering insights into their role as moral advisors and agents.

item.title: Researchers propose failure-driven self-improvement for computer-use agents using LLMs to diagnose and patch errors, improving OpenCUA-72B success rate from 42.3% to 48.9% without extra training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a failure-driven self-improvement approach for computer-use agents that utilize multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to perform tasks on computers. Unlike traditional methods that focus only on successful task completions, this new method leverages failed attempts by using an LLM to diagnose errors, suggest solutions, and generate code patches that improve the agent's performance. Testing this approach on the OpenCUA-72B model with the OSWorld benchmark increased the success rate from 42.3% to 48.9% without additional training and with minimal inference overhead. This approach complements existing success-based training pipelines by extracting valuable insights from failure cases, which are typically discarded. The process involves human verification of generated patches to ensure quality improvements. The results demonstrate that incorporating failure analysis can lead to more efficient and effective enhancements in agent capabilities, offering a promising direction for future development of computer-use agents.

item.title: Researchers find probability calibration reduces evaluator preference coupling in LLM agent feedback loops by up to 49%, improving strategy learning accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that applying probability calibration to evaluator feedback in large language model (LLM) agent training can significantly reduce evaluator preference coupling, a bias where evaluator judgments skew the agent's learned strategies. In a controlled experiment comparing standard binary feedback with confidence-calibrated updates, calibration lowered the coupling coefficient by 20-49% and reduced divergence measures by 45-67%, indicating more accurate strategy learning. The study used DeepSeek-V4-Pro as the executor and GLM5.2 as the evaluator, confirming that the improvements were not due to reduced update asymmetry through a symmetric logistic regression control. The authors have released the calibrated training protocol and suggest it as an effective, lightweight method to mitigate evaluator bias in LLM feedback loops, enhancing the reliability of LLM-as-judge deployment systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce STEB, an open-source Style Text Embedding Benchmark covering 96 datasets in 7 languages to standardize style embedding evaluation across multiple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced the Style Text Embedding Benchmark (STEB), an open-source framework designed to standardize the evaluation of style embeddings across various tasks. STEB includes 96 datasets in seven languages and covers applications such as authorship verification, authorship retrieval, AI-text detection, and linguistic feature probing. The benchmark reveals that semantic embeddings generally perform poorly on stylistic tasks and that no single style embedding excels universally across all evaluated tasks. STEB aims to address the fragmented nature of style embedding evaluation by providing a comprehensive and consistent testing ground. The researchers have made the STEB codebase publicly available to facilitate further research and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce QVal, a training-free testbed to cheaply evaluate dense supervision signals for long-horizon LLM agents across 21 methods and multiple environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced QVal, a training-free testbed designed to evaluate dense supervision signals for long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents. QVal assesses how well a method's scoring aligns with the Q-values of a strong reference policy, enabling direct comparison of supervision signals without the need for costly training pipelines. This approach addresses the challenge of sparse outcome-only rewards by providing a way to evaluate intermediate action quality across various methods and environments. QVal-v1.0 benchmarks 21 dense supervision methods spanning seven methodological families across four diverse environments and six open-weight model backbones, conducting over 1,200 evaluation experiments. The study found that simple prompting baselines often outperform recent dense supervision techniques, with performance clustering by method family. QVal is designed for easy extension to new environments and methods, facilitating iterative development of dense supervision approaches prior to training.

item.title: Researchers find language models trained on fixed counterfactual explanations produce introspective behavior tracking shifts without updated supervision across multiple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that language models (LMs) trained to generate explanations of their predictions using fixed counterfactual explanations from earlier model checkpoints or similar models can produce explanations that more accurately reflect their current behavior than the original training targets. This phenomenon, termed "introspective coupling," occurs when the training explanations remain correlated with the model's evolving behavior, allowing explanations to track behavioral changes even without updated supervision. The effect was observed across multiple tasks, including sycophancy and refusal, and demonstrated robustness to label noise. The study shows that fixed datasets of counterfactual explanations can serve as scalable and generalizable signals for post-training introspection, enabling LMs to adapt their explanations alongside shifts in behavior when trained concurrently with other objectives. This insight suggests a promising approach for improving the faithfulness of model-generated explanations without requiring continuous retraining on updated supervision data.

item.title: Researchers introduce DeXposure-Claw, an agentic system using forecast-grounded LLM supervision for DeFi risk management with regulator-aligned evaluation on five years of data [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DeXposure-Claw, an agentic supervision system designed to manage risks in decentralized finance (DeFi) by using forecast-grounded large language model (LLM) supervision aligned with regulatory standards. The system integrates a graph time-series foundation model to predict future exposure networks, deterministic monitors and stress scenarios to generate alerts and evidence, and confidence gates to control escalation, ultimately producing auditable supervisory tickets with clear rationales. This approach addresses the limitations of general-purpose LLM agents, which tend to overreact to weak evidence and recommend unnecessary high-stakes interventions. The team also introduced DeXposure-Bench, a comprehensive evaluation framework that measures the system's decisions against regulator-aligned criteria, including absolute loss and false-intervention rates. Experiments conducted on five years of weekly real-world data demonstrate the effectiveness of DeXposure-Claw in providing reliable and accountable DeFi risk supervision. The code for the system is publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Survey presents unified framework and taxonomy for AI-generated game commentary, reviewing methods, datasets, and challenges in live observation, strategic analysis, and historical recall [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new survey presents a unified framework and taxonomy for AI-Generated Game Commentary (AI-GGC), organizing this emerging research area around three core commentator capabilities: Live Observation, Strategic Analysis, and Historical Recall. It categorizes commentary into Descriptive, Analytical, and Background types, providing a comprehensive review of existing methods, datasets, and evaluation metrics while assessing their strengths and limitations. The survey also identifies key challenges and suggests promising directions for future research in AI-GGC, aiming to consolidate fragmented studies and advance the field systematically.

item.title: Researchers propose GUI-AIMA, an attention-based fine-tuning framework aligning intrinsic multimodal attention for efficient GUI grounding with state-of-the-art accuracy on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced GUI-AIMA, a novel attention-based fine-tuning framework designed to improve graphical user interface (GUI) grounding by aligning intrinsic multimodal attention in large language models. Unlike traditional methods that generate precise screen coordinates from visual inputs, GUI-AIMA identifies relevant visual patches first and then determines exact click locations, enhancing efficiency and accuracy without relying on coordinate generation. This approach leverages the native grounding ability found in the attention maps of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and adapts patch-wise grounding signals through multi-head aggregation. Trained on a relatively small dataset of 509,000 samples, GUI-AIMA-3B demonstrates exceptional data efficiency and achieves state-of-the-art performance among 3B parameter models across multiple benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-v2, OSWorld-G, MMBench-GUI-L2, and UI-Vision. Its coordinate-free design also supports an optional zoom-in stage, further enhancing its flexibility and precision in GUI grounding tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce TaNOS, a self-supervised pretraining framework that improves numerical reasoning robustness and transferability on expert-domain tables, outperforming GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro in FinQA benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TaNOS, a self-supervised pretraining framework designed to enhance numerical reasoning over expert-domain tables by improving robustness and transferability. TaNOS employs header anonymization, operation sketches, and a program-first self-supervised approach to reduce reliance on superficial cues and promote structural reasoning. When applied to an 8-billion-parameter instruction-tuned model, TaNOS achieved 80.13% execution accuracy on the FinQA benchmark using only 10% of the training data, outperforming traditional supervised fine-tuning methods and proprietary models like GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro. TaNOS also demonstrated strong resilience to domain shifts, showing less than a 2 percentage point drop in accuracy across different domains, compared to over 10 points for standard fine-tuning approaches. These findings suggest that combining structural guidance with header-agnostic representations and correctness-guaranteed self-supervision can significantly improve the robustness and generalization of numerical reasoning models across diverse expert tables.

item.title: Researchers identify shared lexical task-specific attention heads in LLMs that explain behavioral variability across instruction-based and example-based prompts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified specific attention heads in large language models (LLMs) that consistently represent task information across different prompting styles, such as instruction-based and example-based prompts. These "lexical task heads" appear to underlie the models' ability to perform tasks and explain why their behavior varies depending on how prompts are presented. The study shows that the activation level of these heads correlates with performance, and failures can result from competing task signals that weaken the intended task representation. By comparing two common prompting methods, the researchers found that despite performance fluctuations, LLMs engage shared internal mechanisms to process tasks. This discovery sheds light on the internal representations driving LLM behavior, offering a clearer understanding of prompt sensitivity that has often seemed unpredictable to users and developers. The findings contribute to explaining how LLMs interpret and respond to different prompt formulations, potentially guiding improvements in model reliability and interpretability.

item.title: Researchers introduce INFUSER, an influence-guided self-evolution framework that improves reasoning in language models with over 20% performance gain on Olympiad and SuperGPQA benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed INFUSER, a novel influence-guided self-evolution framework designed to enhance reasoning capabilities in pretrained language models. INFUSER employs an iterative co-training approach involving a Generator that creates questions and answers from unstructured documents, and a Solver that improves by training on these generated examples. This method uses an optimizer-aware influence score to reward the Generator for producing questions that effectively improve the Solver, resulting in over 20% performance gains on Olympiad and SuperGPQA benchmarks compared to existing self-evolution techniques. The framework introduces DuGRPO, a dual-normalized variant of GRPO, to better handle the noisy influence scores during training. INFUSER's adaptive curriculum prioritizes questions that are beneficial to the Solver rather than merely difficult ones. Experiments demonstrate that an 8-billion-parameter INFUSER Generator surpasses a frozen 32-billion-parameter baseline on math and coding tasks. Additional tests confirm the necessity of each component, and extensions show the framework's flexibility and generalizability. The code for INFUSER is publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers introduce Sibling-Guided Credit Distillation to improve long-horizon tool-use reinforcement learning by guiding credit assignment while maintaining policy gradient control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Sibling-Guided Credit Distillation (SGCD), a new method to enhance long-horizon tool-use reinforcement learning by improving credit assignment while maintaining policy gradient control. SGCD uses distillation to provide bounded credit weighting rather than competing with the actor loss, leveraging dynamic sampling of mixed successful and failed rollouts and an external language model to guide training. This approach leads to better performance on benchmark tasks compared to existing methods. SGCD was tested on the AppWorld and tau^3-airline environments, showing improvements in held-out evaluation scores over GRPO-family comparators. The method reshapes token-level advantages based on teacher-student divergence, while the deployed model operates with only the clean task prompt. These results suggest a design principle for long-horizon tool-use agents: use distillation to guide credit assignment but keep policy gradient as the primary driver of actor updates.

item.title: Researchers present HASTE, a hierarchical multi-agent system that organizes ML engineering skills across global, domain, and competition tiers to improve transfer efficiency and medal rates in Kaggle competitions [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HASTE, a hierarchical multi-agent system designed to improve machine learning engineering efficiency by organizing skills across global, domain, and competition-specific tiers. This system coordinates specialized agents and uses large language model-driven abstraction to facilitate knowledge transfer, significantly increasing medal rates in Kaggle competitions compared to flat skill loading methods. HASTE achieved a 77.3% medal rate on the MLE-Bench Lite benchmark, demonstrating its effectiveness in both cold-start and warm-start scenarios. The system maintains a 159-skill inventory and shows that tiered loading leads to a 100% medal rate across eight competitions, outperforming flat loading which only reached 62.5%. Warm-start runs, which reuse skills from previous competitions, require 52% fewer refinement iterations and result in a higher acceptance rate of proposed changes by the agents. These findings suggest that structured knowledge organization can enhance ML engineering performance, potentially reducing the need for stronger models or larger compute budgets.

item.title: Researchers propose RoPoLL, a robust panel of LLM judges using geometric median aggregation, outperforming traditional PoLL under biased contamination across multiple benchmarks and corruption regimes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced RoPoLL, a robust panel of large language model (LLM) judges that improves upon the traditional Panel of LLM Evaluators (PoLL) by using geometric median aggregation to achieve greater resistance to biased contamination. Unlike PoLL, which can suffer unbounded bias when even a single judge exhibits typical LLM failures such as mode collapse or sycophancy, RoPoLL employs a robust mean estimator that maintains accuracy under various corruption scenarios. This approach has been tested across multiple benchmarks, judge sizes, and corruption regimes, demonstrating superior performance especially against biased and heavy-tailed adversarial attacks. The study formalizes the LLM Jury under the Huber contamination model and provides theoretical error bounds that align with information-theoretic limits. Experiments involving 13 open-weight judges and several reward-model benchmarks show that RoPoLL consistently outperforms PoLL, achieving up to 19% improvement on cross-dimensional attacks and significantly better results against Byzantine adversaries. Notably, a small RoPoLL committee with fewer parameters outperformed a much larger model on a benchmark with substantial corruption, confirming its robustness to biased contamination rather than mere noise. These findings suggest that RoPoLL offers a more reliable and computationally feasible method for aggregating LLM evaluations, potentially enhancing the robustness of AI model assessment in the presence of adversarial or biased inputs. This advancement could influence future evaluation protocols and improve the trustworthiness of consensus-based LLM judgments.

item.title: Researchers introduce Neuro-Bayesian-Symbolic Residual Attention Shallow Network for explainable cybersecurity risk assessment, validated on 20 open-source projects with confidence scores of 0.79-0.97 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Neuro-Bayesian-Symbolic Residual Attention Shallow Network (NBS-RASN), a hybrid neural architecture designed for explainable cybersecurity risk assessment in open-source ecosystems. This shallow network integrates domain knowledge, causal reasoning, and expert judgment through 80 interpretable neurons across 12 layers, enforcing five epistemological axioms to ensure precision, causality, falsifiability, transparency, and completeness. Unlike traditional deep models, NBS-RASN maintains interpretability while learning complex risk patterns using residual attention and feedback loops, producing fully decomposable risk scores that include expert adjustments linked to specific risk amplifiers. The model was validated on 20 open-source projects covering all OWASP Top 10:2025 categories and various language risk classes, achieving confidence scores between 0.79 and 0.97. This approach challenges the notion that deep learning requires deep networks by demonstrating that shallow networks with embedded deep reasoning can outperform opaque models in cybersecurity contexts where interpretability is critical.

item.title: Researchers evaluate natural-language-to-Lean statement formalization on a 400-entry graduate-level benchmark, finding 89.5% compilation but only 60.5% consensus faithfulness, highlighting gaps in current formalizer models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated the process of converting natural language statements into formal Lean language on a 400-entry graduate-level benchmark covering topics like real analysis, complex analysis, topology, and algebra. Their study revealed that while 89.5% of the formalized statements compiled successfully, only 60.5% were deemed faithful to the original meaning by consensus, highlighting a significant gap between syntactic validity and semantic accuracy. The evaluation combined Lean compilation checks, cross-model semantic judgments, and expert human calibration to assess faithfulness. Human audits confirmed that most consensus-positive outputs were indeed faithful, while many compile-passing but consensus-negative outputs contained semantic errors. The study also analyzed the impact of different formalization pipeline components, finding that elaboration feedback improved validity but increased semantic failures, search enhanced grounding and selectivity, and expert drafting was largely replaceable when feedback and grounding were present. These findings suggest that formal validity, proof-oriented Lean competence, and faithful statement generation are distinct challenges that should be evaluated separately. Current one-shot formalizer models and prover-oriented Lean models show limited performance in faithful statement generation, indicating room for improvement in natural-language-to-formal-language translation tools.

item.title: Researchers introduce HealthAgentBench, a benchmark suite of 54 realistic healthcare AI tasks across 7 categories, revealing current frontier agents achieve only about 42% success rate [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HealthAgentBench, a comprehensive benchmark suite comprising 54 realistic healthcare AI tasks across seven categories designed to evaluate the capabilities of advanced AI agents in clinical workflows. The suite challenges agents to perform complex, multi-step reasoning using raw healthcare data in diverse environments, reflecting real-world patient care scenarios. Testing leading AI models revealed a modest overall success rate of about 42%, highlighting the difficulty of these tasks and the current limitations of frontier AI agents in healthcare applications. HealthAgentBench covers a wide range of healthcare workflows and modalities, including electronic health records and medical imaging. While some agents showed promise in automating research modeling pipelines with EHR data, medical imaging tasks remain particularly challenging. The benchmark also identified that tasks requiring extensive search and compositional reasoning are difficult for all tested agents, indicating areas needing further development. The introduction of HealthAgentBench provides a rigorous and realistic platform for assessing AI progress in healthcare, emphasizing significant room for improvement. By releasing this benchmark publicly, the researchers aim to foster advancements in AI agents capable of handling complex clinical tasks, ultimately supporting better healthcare outcomes.

item.title: Researchers propose Hard-Routed MoR-LoRA, a two-stage framework for composing frozen reasoning LoRA experts with hard top-1 routing, reducing trainable parameters and preserving expert behavior across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Hard-Routed MoR-LoRA, a two-stage framework designed to compose frozen reasoning LoRA experts using hard top-1 routing. This approach enables the integration of independently trained domain-specific LoRA adapters into a single large language model while preserving their original behavior and significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters compared to soft-routing mixture methods. The method involves first training domain-specific LoRA adapters with reinforcement learning to develop reasoning experts. These experts are then frozen, and a lightweight shared router along with a small attention LoRA is trained to select exactly one expert per token through hard routing. Experiments across multiple benchmarks and model scales demonstrate that Hard-Routed MoR-LoRA maintains expert performance efficiently, with analysis indicating that hard unit-scale routing offers a simpler and more effective way to compose frozen LoRA experts than normalized soft mixtures.

item.title: Researchers introduce CDR-Bench, a benchmark with 3,462 tasks to evaluate LLMs' execution of compositional, order-sensitive data refinement recipes, revealing sharp performance drops in complex settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CDR-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on their ability to execute compositional, order-sensitive data refinement tasks. The benchmark includes 3,462 tasks across four real-world domains and 29 operators, assessing models in atomic, order-agnostic, and order-sensitive scenarios with deterministic reference outputs for precise evaluation. Testing over ten state-of-the-art LLMs revealed significant performance declines in complex, compositional settings, especially when task order mattered, indicating current models struggle with procedural accuracy in data refinement. CDR-Bench addresses a gap in existing evaluations by focusing specifically on multi-step data refinement recipes where both the composition and sequence of operations impact the final result. Unlike prior benchmarks that separate text editing from code or tool execution, this benchmark provides a comprehensive and exact framework to measure LLMs' faithful execution of these tasks. The findings highlight consistent failure patterns, emphasizing the need for improved model capabilities in handling procedural and order-dependent data processing.

item.title: Researchers propose a prediction-error surprise signal to gate plasticity and support metacognition in episodic memory and vision-language models, demonstrating improved retention and concept recognition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a prediction-error surprise signal that functions as both a gate for neural plasticity and a basis for metacognition in artificial intelligence systems. This approach was tested in two settings: an episodic memory system that selectively writes new concepts when surprise is high and consolidates them through offline replay, and a vision-language model that uses the surprise signal to modulate its responses based on familiarity with concepts. The episodic memory system demonstrated improved retention and few-shot learning performance on ImageNet classes, while the vision-language model effectively distinguished known from novel concepts and learned new concepts from single user interactions.

item.title: Cohere and LG CNS develop LuckyStar 111B, a 111B-parameter multilingual reasoning model for Korean-English enterprise agents with efficient tool use and memory-constrained deployment [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Cohere and LG CNS have developed LuckyStar 111B, a 111-billion-parameter hybrid reasoning model designed for Korean-English enterprise agents that operate under practical memory and serving constraints. The model builds on Cohere's post-trained Command A model and employs preamble conditioning to alternate between concise non-reasoning and extended tool-oriented reasoning modes. It incorporates multilingual supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, language-consistency rewards for Korean responses, and 4-bit quantization to enable efficient single-GPU deployment. The adapted model enhances mathematical reasoning, function calling, and natural-language-to-SQL (NL2SQL) capabilities while maintaining strong instruction-following performance in both Korean and English. This work offers a practical approach and analysis for adapting post-trained multilingual models to verifiable agentic workflows within memory-limited environments, supporting more effective enterprise applications.

item.title: Researchers introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS) to improve multimodal large language model safety using textual refusal directions without multimodal safety data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a novel approach to enhance safety in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) without relying on multimodal safety data. MARS leverages textual refusal directions extracted from the language model backbone, which generalize across different modalities such as images and videos. This method addresses challenges in existing safety techniques that require difficult-to-obtain unsafe multimodal data by correcting modality misalignment and adaptively controlling steering strength during model output generation. The approach operates by re-centering activations, selecting optimal intervention layers, and applying steering at the first generated token, enabling consistent safety improvements while maintaining model utility. Evaluations on five state-of-the-art MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak benchmarks demonstrate MARS's effectiveness. These findings suggest that safety-related structures are shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions offer a promising foundation for multimodal alignment.

item.title: Researchers find self-generated question-answer training for language models is fragile due to biased question selection and instruction compliance, propose fixes reducing bias and injection compliance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified fragility in the process of training language models using self-generated question-answer (QA) pairs. They found that the question generation step is biased, focusing on certain salient parts of a document and influenced by local presentation, which can lead to artifacts like poorly cleaned markup dominating the training data. Additionally, models tend to comply with instruction-like passages embedded in the text when generating answers, especially under conflicting tasks, with larger models showing higher compliance. The study reveals that these issues stem from the implicit policies in QA generation rather than the training loop itself. By linking each question to a fixed target and filtering out instruction-like spans before answering, the researchers significantly reduced bias and instruction compliance, lowering mean injection compliance from 88% to 13% while preserving most of the clean text. These findings suggest practical methods to improve the robustness of self-supervised training for language models.

item.title: Researchers present PolicyGuard, a neuro-symbolic framework converting organizational policies into executable compliance review engines using LLMs and symbolic evaluation for NDA contract analysis [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PolicyGuard, a neuro-symbolic framework that transforms organizational policies into executable compliance review engines. This system uses large language models (LLMs) to interpret documents and answer specific extraction questions, while a symbolic evaluator applies formal logic rules to assess compliance. PolicyGuard was tested on company-specific non-disclosure agreement (NDA) reviews, ensuring contract clauses adhere to internal negotiation policies. By separating policy formalization, document interpretation, and compliance evaluation, PolicyGuard enhances transparency, maintainability, and testability in policy-grounded document reviews. This approach addresses limitations of end-to-end prompting with LLMs, where policy logic remains implicit and difficult to inspect or update.

item.title: Researchers propose ASR-agnostic multimodal spectrotemporal model using Mel spectrograms for early dementia detection, achieving up to 93.7% accuracy on Slovak and Spanish datasets with cross-lingual validation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an ASR-agnostic multimodal model that uses Mel spectrograms to detect early signs of dementia, achieving up to 93.7% accuracy on Slovak and Spanish datasets. The model captures shifting spectral energy patterns as digital biomarkers of cognitive decline and integrates these with acoustic embeddings through a cross-attention mechanism and Transformer encoder. This approach avoids reliance on transcription and preserves temporal structure, addressing limitations of previous speech-based dementia detection systems. The team trained independent models on English, Slovak, and Spanish corpora, finding that the Slovak model performed best, while the English baseline showed lower accuracy due to known recording artifacts. Cross-lingual studies revealed that the effectiveness of multimodal fusion depends on the dataset, being crucial when signals are distributed across modalities but less beneficial or even counterproductive when one modality dominates or no signal exists. The model's auxiliary temporal losses converged to language-invariant values, indicating architectural stability across languages.

item.title: Researchers present a physician-guided interactive machine learning framework for delirium detection using 3,862 hospital admissions, showing improved accuracy and temporal robustness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a physician-guided interactive machine learning framework to improve the detection of delirium in hospitalized patients. Using data from 3,862 admissions across six Toronto hospitals, the framework integrates clinical and administrative information with physician input to refine features and enhance model interpretability. This approach demonstrated better accuracy and temporal robustness compared to automated methods, highlighting clinically relevant signals through explainable AI techniques. The study utilized the General Medicine Inpatient Initiative (GEMINI) dataset, incorporating variables such as laboratory results, medications, and radiology-derived text indicators. Physicians actively participated in feature selection and model evaluation, with Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) used to clarify feature contributions. The framework was tested using temporally separated holdout and validation cohorts, confirming its effectiveness over baseline classifiers. These findings support the use of a human-in-the-loop machine learning approach as a practical tool for delirium detection in clinical settings, potentially aiding in earlier identification and improved patient care.

item.title: Researchers propose a causal inference framework to estimate coupon timing effectiveness using natural randomized control trials, validated on onboarding and retention campaigns
item.description: Researchers have developed a causal inference framework to evaluate the impact of coupon timing on user engagement without the need for dedicated A/B testing. By leveraging "natural randomized control trials," the framework measures how delivering coupons at critical moments in the customer journey affects their effectiveness. The approach was validated through a user onboarding coupon campaign within the researchers' company and further tested on a publicly available dataset related to user retention. This method addresses the challenge of implementing real-time event-triggered coupon distribution, which can be costly, by providing a data-driven way to assess timing effects using existing data. The framework's successful application in different campaign contexts demonstrates its potential for guiding marketing decisions and improving coupon strategies across various stages of the customer lifecycle.

item.title: Researchers show minimal LLM agent collectives spontaneously develop cooperative behaviors and evolving cultural artifacts using shared decaying text stores and simple tools [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied collectives of three large language model (LLM) agents operating with minimal context, prompting, and simple tools, allowing them to communicate and manipulate a shared, actively decaying text store. This setup introduced evolutionary pressure, leading the agents to spontaneously develop cooperative behaviors, storage management strategies, and complex evolving cultural artifacts without any top-down design. Analysis using dynamical systems tools revealed that these behaviors exhibited structured long-range coherence beyond the entropy limits of the decaying store, aligning with the concept of emergent culture as defined by Sperber. The study draws inspiration from swarm engineering and demonstrates that even minimal LLM systems can generate sophisticated collective dynamics through simple interactions and shared resources. The findings suggest that such emergent cultural phenomena arise naturally from the agents' interactions with the decaying text environment, highlighting new possibilities for understanding and designing multi-agent AI systems.

item.title: Researchers propose a multimodal framework combining ASR embeddings and LLM-augmented linguistic features for early dementia detection, achieving over 89% F1-scores on ADReSS datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multimodal framework that combines acoustic speech representations and linguistic features enhanced by a large language model (LLM) to detect early signs of dementia. Using Whisper for automatic speech recognition, the system extracts both acoustic embeddings and transcripts, which are then analyzed through temporal networks and LLM prompts to capture diverse linguistic markers. This approach achieved F1-scores exceeding 89% on the ADReSS datasets, demonstrating effective integration of acoustic and linguistic data for dementia screening. The framework employs attention pooling to convert variable-length acoustic sequences into fixed-dimensional embeddings, while the LLM extracts interpretable linguistic features such as lexical diversity, syntactic complexity, semantic coherence, and discourse patterns. A gated fusion network combines these modalities, and ablation studies confirm that the multimodal fusion outperforms using either acoustic or linguistic features alone, highlighting the benefit of integrating both types of biomarkers for improved detection accuracy.

item.title: Researchers propose a deep reinforcement learning method for locker-based truck-drone routing integrating pickups, deliveries, and no-fly zones to minimize operational costs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a deep reinforcement learning approach to optimize locker-based truck-drone delivery systems, addressing the complex coordination of pickups, deliveries, drone battery constraints, and no-fly zones. Their method models the routing problem as a Markov Decision Process and employs a two-stage neural heuristic to minimize operational costs for fleets of drone-equipped trucks. The first stage solves the truck-only routing problem using an attention-based encoder and a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit decoder, while the second stage integrates a policy-transfer strategy with a hybrid dispatch heuristic to coordinate truck and drone routes effectively. Experiments demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing metaheuristic and neural heuristic methods across various scales, offering a scalable and efficient solution under practical delivery constraints.

item.title: Researchers define a coherence-based training law for noisy U(1)-equivariant quantum neural networks, linking sector coherence to gradient trainability under decoherence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a coherence-based training law that explains how gradients in U(1)-equivariant quantum neural networks remain trainable despite the presence of noise and decoherence. By analyzing brickwork circuits that conserve charge, they identified two key factors influencing gradient trainability: causality, which confines the gradient to a specific sector, and coherence, which governs the rate of gradient decay through off-diagonal sector modes observable by the readout. This work establishes a light-cone reduction and defines a coherence rate that predicts gradient behavior under noise. The team validated their theoretical findings through density-matrix simulations, showing that gradient degradation under noise follows a predictable pattern based on noise depth and coherence contraction. Notably, their training law accurately predicted no gradient loss in a correlated-dephasing noise channel, outperforming standard diagnostic methods. This study highlights readout-visible sector coherence as the critical quantity linking equivariant quantum architectures, open-system dynamics, and the ability to train quantum neural networks in noisy environments.

item.title: Researchers present BEST-RQ-2, a two-step contextualize-then-predict approach for self-supervised audio representations that improves transfer performance on X-ARES benchmarks while maintaining inference efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed BEST-RQ-2, an advanced self-supervised learning method for audio representation that improves transfer performance across various audio domains while maintaining efficient inference. This approach introduces a two-step process where a Vision Transformer (ViT) context encoder analyzes unmasked spectrogram regions, and a lightweight predictor estimates targets for masked regions, which is then discarded after pretraining. BEST-RQ-2 outperforms previous one-stage models on the X-ARES and XARES-LLM benchmarks, particularly enhancing performance in music and environmental sound recognition with minimal impact on speech tasks. The method builds on the original BEST-RQ by retaining frozen random-projection-based discrete targets and replacing the Conformer encoder with a ViT, which shifts performance across domains. The key innovation lies in separating contextualization and prediction stages during masked audio modeling, leading to better overall transfer capabilities without increasing computational costs during inference. The researchers have made the code and model checkpoints publicly available to support further development in the field.

item.title: Researchers introduce NHANES Accelerometry Cardiometabolic Benchmark using 1,381 adults' data to predict cardiometabolic risk biomarkers with uncertainty quantification and subgroup fairness analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the NHANES Accelerometry Cardiometabolic Benchmark using data from 1,381 adults collected between 2003 and 2006, including hip-worn accelerometry, fasting laboratory biomarkers, dietary intake, and anthropometric measurements. They evaluated three machine learning methods-ridge regression, XGBoost, and TabPFN v2-to predict cardiometabolic risk biomarkers such as glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting triglycerides, and C-reactive protein (CRP). TabPFN v2 showed the best overall predictive performance, particularly for HbA1c and CRP, while triglycerides remained difficult to predict, aligning with known genetic influences. The study applied split conformal prediction to generate 90% prediction intervals and assessed fairness across demographic subgroups defined by sex and race/ethnicity. While overall coverage met the target for HbA1c and CRP, some subgroups, such as Mexican American participants for HbA1c, experienced undercoverage, highlighting challenges in achieving equitable clinical predictions. The benchmark and associated code are publicly available for further research and validation.

item.title: Researchers identify geometric cause for failure of few-step deterministic generation on continuous text latents versus success on image latents, linking decoder sharpness to token flipping and proposing accuracy-depth-stiffness tradeoffs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a geometric reason why deterministic few-step generation works well on continuous image latents but fails on continuous text latents, leading to incoherent text output. They found that the failure is due to the inability of a smooth deterministic map to resolve discrete branch choices before a sharp categorical readout, making decoder sharpness the key factor rather than transport accuracy. Their analysis includes proofs showing how token flipping occurs near decision boundaries and introduces diagnostics that reveal continuous-text decoders amplify boundary perturbations significantly more than image decoders. The study also explores mechanisms that can overcome these limitations, such as categorical commitment in autoregressive decoders and stochastic re-injection methods. Additionally, the researchers present theoretical results on the relationship between latent dimension, mode separation, and the required deterministic stiffness, outlining an accuracy-depth-stiffness tradeoff inherent in deterministic continuous models. These findings clarify fundamental constraints in text latent generation and suggest directions for improving model design beyond deterministic continuous approaches.

item.title: Researchers introduce Hierarchical Global Attention as a drop-in replacement for dense causal attention in pretrained long-context transformers, enabling 64K-token context on single RTX 5090 without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Hierarchical Global Attention (HGA), a method that replaces dense causal attention in pretrained long-context transformers without requiring retraining or changes to existing model parameters. Implemented on the Qwen3-30B model running on a single RTX 5090 GPU, HGA enables processing of up to 64,000 tokens by using a two-level hierarchical routing system that efficiently retrieves relevant token chunks and performs exact attention on a reduced subset. This approach significantly lowers GPU memory usage by storing most token data in host RAM or NVMe storage and transferring only a small working set to the GPU during attention. HGA's hierarchical retrieval first selects relevant chunks using compact summaries aware of positional encoding, then refines this selection before applying token-level attention. This method maintains attention accuracy within 0.01 to 0.02 nats of dense attention across context lengths from 4,000 to 64,000 tokens, while using only about 3% of tokens in the routed attention. The results indicate that the minor approximation introduced by hierarchical routing has minimal impact on performance, with remaining quality differences likely due to positional encoding limitations rather than the routing technique itself.

item.title: Researchers deploy automated pipeline to optimize enterprise AI skill descriptions, matching manual accuracy with 32x less engineering effort and identifying limits of text-level fixes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an automated pipeline to optimize natural language skill descriptions used by enterprise AI agents to route user queries. This system addresses the problem of skill collision, where overlapping descriptions cause misrouting, by producing optimized descriptions that match the accuracy of manually tuned ones while reducing engineering effort by 32 times. The pipeline was tested on a production group chat agent with nine skills, achieving an average F1 score of 79.2%, comparable to the 79.4% from manual tuning.

item.title: Researchers introduce Indi-RomCoM benchmark to evaluate large language models on Romanized Indic-English code-mixed instructions across seven tasks and four languages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Indi-RomCoM, a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on Romanized Indic-English code-mixed instructions. This benchmark covers seven instruction-following tasks across four widely spoken Indic languages and includes varying levels of code-mixing intensity. The study reveals that LLMs generally underperform on these code-mixed instructions, with performance declining as the density of code-mixing increases. The evaluation involved a range of LLMs, including proprietary, open-weight, and Indic-focused models, tested under zero- and few-shot settings. Notably, reasoning tasks showed less performance degradation compared to detection tasks like toxicity identification, likely because generated explanations provide additional context. Indi-RomCoM aims to support the development of more inclusive multilingual AI systems capable of handling the prevalent Romanized code-mixing communication style in multilingual communities.

item.title: Researchers introduce Gradient Smoothing, a depth-wise gradient augmentation method that improves optimization and generalization across diverse neural network architectures and training regimes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Gradient Smoothing, a novel depth-wise gradient augmentation technique designed to enhance optimization and generalization in deep neural networks with repeated architectural blocks like transformers. This method transforms layer-wise optimizer updates along the depth dimension, improving training performance without altering model architectures or objectives. Gradient Smoothing is compatible with various base optimizers and incurs minimal computational overhead. The approach was tested across diverse architectures and training scenarios, including language model pretraining, reinforcement learning post-training for large language models, diffusion modeling, and image classification with Vision Transformers. Results show consistent improvements in both optimization and generalization, alongside promoting more structured representation evolution across network depth, supporting its role as a structured depth-wise preconditioning method. This establishes Depth-wise Gradient Augmentation as a promising framework for leveraging cross-depth structure in neural network optimization.

item.title: Researchers evaluate GPT-2 models trained on 'impossible' language variants, finding gradual grammatical sensitivity decline but significant generative failures linked to non-attestation in human languages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated how GPT-2 style transformer models perform when trained on "impossible" variants of English-languages considered unlearnable by humans. They assessed two hypotheses: whether these models struggle due to reduced grammatical sensitivity or difficulties in generating language. The study found that while grammatical sensitivity declined gradually depending on the language's structure, the models showed significant failures in producing high-quality, longer sentences. The experiments used BLiMP minimal pairs to measure grammaticality sensitivity and revealed that the models' generative capabilities deteriorated more sharply than their grammatical understanding. These findings suggest that the inability to generate coherent language may explain why such "impossible" languages do not appear in human linguistic systems, linking model behavior to linguistic non-attestation through generative deficiencies and transmission failures.

item.title: Researchers develop stationary-distribution theory modeling Random Forest ensemble size tuning as a birth-death Markov chain with stochastic plateau behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a stationary-distribution theory to model the tuning of ensemble size in Random Forest algorithms using a birth-death Markov chain framework. This approach addresses the plateau-based tuning method, which adjusts the number of trees by comparing out-of-bag scores at geometric triplets of tree counts. Instead of converging to a fixed value, the ensemble size fluctuates around a stationary regime, which the new theory characterizes mathematically. The study models the central ensemble size as a birth-death Markov chain on a geometric grid and derives its stationary distribution through local balance equations. Using approximations such as the folded-normal and Gaussian models, the researchers describe the equilibrium behavior, variance, and spread of the ensemble size during tuning. Their findings reinterpret plateau-based Random Forest tuning as a stochastic process rather than a deterministic stopping rule, providing deeper insight into the dynamics of ensemble size selection.

item.title: Researchers introduce GradeSQL framework using Outcome Reward Models for test-time verification in Text-to-SQL, improving accuracy by up to 4.33% on BIRD and 2.10% on Spider benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed GradeSQL, a new framework that uses Outcome Reward Models (ORMs) for test-time verification in Text-to-SQL tasks, enhancing the accuracy of large language models during inference. By training task-specific ORMs through automated candidate generation and execution-based labeling, GradeSQL enables effective verification without manual annotation. This approach outperforms traditional heuristic methods like Best-of-N sampling and Majority Voting, achieving accuracy improvements of up to 4.33% on the BIRD benchmark and 2.10% on the Spider benchmark. The study evaluated GradeSQL across multiple open-source large language model families and demonstrated that ORM-based selection scales well with larger candidate sets and yields stronger gains on complex queries. These results suggest that ORM-based verification offers a simple, scalable, and more semantically informed alternative to existing test-time selection strategies for structured query generation in Text-to-SQL. The researchers have made their code, datasets, and models publicly available to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers introduce Turing Test Network for zero-shot pseudo-label pruning, improving label accuracy and enabling task transfer across vision-language models with up to 44% F1-score gains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Turing-inspired Label Imitation Game (LIG) and its associated Turing Test Network (TTN) to improve the accuracy of zero-shot pseudo-labeling in vision-language models. This approach treats pseudo-label pruning as an adversarial process, using a task-agnostic network to evaluate labels within a dataset-wide context rather than relying on fixed thresholds. Experiments on four diverse datasets show that the TTN consistently enhances label accuracy across three state-of-the-art models without requiring additional supervision or retraining. The TTN leverages learned semantic-contextual logic as an alternative to traditional spatial-geometric verification, enabling zero-shot task transfer where a model trained on image classification can effectively prune pseudo-labels for object detection. This method yields significant F1-score improvements, with gains of up to 44% after task-specific fine-tuning. Additionally, the TTN helps recover performance on classes that previously had zero recall by refining the training signal, a phenomenon termed Category Revival. The pre-trained TTN models and code have been made publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce TheraJudge and TheraAgent, multi-agent systems using human-aligned evaluation to improve therapeutic quality of mental health language models with strong clinician agreement [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TheraJudge and TheraAgent, a two-stage multi-agent system designed to enhance the therapeutic quality of mental health language models by using human-aligned evaluation as an active control mechanism. TheraJudge is an open-source evaluator trained on human-annotated data to reliably assess responses across seven psychological dimensions, achieving strong agreement with clinician ratings. TheraAgent uses these evaluations to iteratively refine responses through specialized roles, resulting in significant improvements in therapeutic quality and safety. TheraJudge demonstrated high intraclass correlation coefficients (0.87-0.95) with clinician assessments, outperforming existing supervised and closed-source evaluators, especially on critical factors like safety, relevance, and empathy. When applied, TheraAgent improved human-rated therapeutic quality by 0.43 points on a 5-point scale and effectively corrected low-quality responses, with a 94% recovery rate for unsafe outputs. The study highlights that aligning mental health language models effectively requires acting on human-aligned evaluations rather than solely enhancing generation capabilities. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further development and validation.

item.title: Researchers prove on-policy distillation outperforms offline behavior cloning for imitation learning with noisy expert feedback, providing theoretical foundations and new algorithms [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that on-policy distillation (OPD) outperforms offline behavior cloning in imitation learning scenarios where expert feedback is noisy. They introduced a noisy expert model to explain why online methods like OPD, which interact with the expert during learning, achieve better performance than offline methods such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Their findings reveal that offline learning from noisy expert trajectories requires exponentially more samples to match the performance of a clean expert, whereas OPD can achieve this with polynomial sample complexity relative to the task horizon. The study provides theoretical foundations and new algorithms supporting these results, including conditions on the noise distribution that enable horizon-free sample complexity. The authors also extend their analysis to cases with unknown corruption when the clean expert is deterministic, offering insights into why OPD is more effective for training language models from imperfect teachers. This work bridges theoretical understanding and practical algorithm design for imitation learning under noisy expert conditions.

item.title: Researchers develop physics-informed conditional normalizing flows for angles-only cislunar orbit determination using Near Rectilinear Halo Orbit data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a physics-informed approach using conditional normalizing flows to improve orbit determination in the cislunar environment. This method estimates the probability distribution of an object's initial state based on angles-only measurements collected over short observation periods, specifically focusing on Near Rectilinear Halo Orbits. By training on perturbed topocentric observations, the model can represent complex, multimodal posterior distributions and generate physics-consistent state hypotheses from new data. The generated state estimates are further refined through nonlinear least-squares minimization, enhancing their accuracy and providing effective initial guesses for traditional orbit determination algorithms. This approach advances generative astrodynamics by combining machine learning techniques with physical modeling to address challenges in space navigation around the Moon.

item.title: Researchers propose a generative framework using compressed latent spaces for motion planning, demonstrating strong performance on nuPlan and Waymo Open Motion Dataset without task-specific training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new generative framework for motion planning that combines deep learning and model-based planning techniques. Their approach uses an autoencoder to compress motion data into a latent space of discrete tokens, enabling efficient search and optimization of motion plans directly within this compressed representation. This method allows for flexible objective functions at test time and produces realistic motion behaviors without requiring task-specific training. The framework was tested on the nuPlan and Waymo Open Motion Dataset, demonstrating strong performance in closed-loop motion planning and multi-agent scenario synthesis. By leveraging the hierarchical structure of the latent space, the approach effectively balances the flexibility and efficiency of model-based planning with the data-driven capabilities of deep learning, offering a unified solution for complex robotic motion tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce Prost-RL, a reinforcement learning framework for micro-ultrasound prostate cancer detection achieving 79% AUROC on 6,607 biopsy cores across five clinical sites [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Prost-RL, a reinforcement learning framework designed to improve prostate cancer detection using micro-ultrasound imaging. Prost-RL addresses challenges in training deep models due to sparse and noisy supervision by learning where to focus attention before decoding images. Tested on 6,607 biopsy cores from 693 patients across five clinical sites, the system achieved a 79% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for core-level detection, outperforming existing methods. Prost-RL integrates a lightweight reinforcement-learning policy with an encoder-decoder model to generate interpretable spatial attention maps that guide cancer likelihood predictions and image classification. The approach includes Adaptive Policy Optimization to stabilize training and a noise-robust objective to handle weak-label noise and improve localization. The model's learned policy highlights biopsy-aligned regions, providing transparent, spatially grounded evidence alongside quantitative risk assessments.

item.title: Researchers identify deductive stereotyping as a fairness failure in large language models and propose Fair-GCG to reduce bias and improve fairness in reasoning and generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a fairness issue in large language models (LLMs) called deductive stereotyping, where models apply broad population-level patterns to individual cases, resulting in logically consistent but socially biased conclusions. To address this, they propose a reasoning-time injection framework and introduce Fair-GCG, a method to discover effective phrases that guide models toward fairness-aware reasoning. Fair-GCG's injection phrases have been shown to improve performance on multiple fairness benchmarks, generalize across different model sizes, enhance fairness in reasoning, reduce bias in open-ended text generation, and transfer effectively to real-world tasks sensitive to fairness concerns.

item.title: Researchers propose OTCache, an Optimal Transport-based framework for geometry-aware caching in diffusion models achieving up to 4.7x acceleration and improved generation fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced OTCache, a training-free framework designed to accelerate diffusion model sampling by predicting caching schedules using an Optimal Transport-based approach. OTCache addresses limitations in existing graph-based caching methods, which assume additive independence and struggle in low inference step regimes. The framework involves generating a high-fidelity reference schedule, conducting a lightweight anchor search under constrained budgets, and predicting schedules for various budgets through quantile interpolation. Experiments on datasets including FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, and HunyuanVideo demonstrate that OTCache achieves acceleration factors of up to 4.7 times while improving generation fidelity compared to state-of-the-art caching methods. This approach offers a novel perspective on enhancing diffusion model efficiency by modeling caching schedules as smooth policy evolutions inspired by Optimal Transport theory.

item.title: Researchers distill knowledge from DeepSeek-R1 to Qwen2.5-7B using Chain-of-Thought training on John O'Bryan Mathematics Competition problems, improving student model accuracy by 4.76 points [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have successfully distilled knowledge from a large reasoning model, DeepSeek-R1, into a smaller student model, Qwen2.5-7B, using Chain-of-Thought training on problems from the John O'Bryan Mathematics Competition. This approach improved the student model's accuracy by 4.76 percentage points, raising it from 64.67% to 69.43% on the competition dataset, and also enhanced its performance on the MATH-500 benchmark to 73.1%. The study highlights the effectiveness of knowledge distillation and fine-tuning techniques in enhancing compact models for mathematical reasoning tasks. The team created a training corpus from historical competition problems spanning 2011 to 2025 using a dual-agent framework and fine-tuned the student model with Low-Rank Adaptation on Apple Silicon hardware. Initial training runs showed overfitting after 200 iterations, leading to multiple shorter training runs to ensure stability. Additionally, the research examined how response length affects answer quality across six reasoning levels, finding that longer responses generally yield higher accuracy, with significant declines observed as response length decreases. These findings demonstrate that Chain-of-Thought distillation can effectively improve the reasoning capabilities of smaller models, and that maintaining sufficient response length is critical for preserving answer quality in mathematical problem-solving. This work offers insights into optimizing compact AI models for complex reasoning tasks while managing computational resources.
