item.title: Researchers propose ADAPT framework to reduce hallucinations in multimodal large language models by aligning text-to-image cross-attention dynamics, achieving 40%-60% reduction across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ADAPT, a novel framework designed to reduce hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by directly addressing the degradation of text-to-image cross-attention during content generation. ADAPT employs three key strategies: a visual anchor for stable spatial grounding, an attention-supervised inference mechanism to detect and correct attention drift, and a Visual Attention Guidance method to align model preferences with visually grounded responses. This approach has demonstrated a 40% to 60% reduction in hallucination rates across multiple benchmarks while maintaining the models' general multimodal capabilities. The study identifies progressive degradation of cross-attention as a core internal signature of hallucination, which leads to unfocused or biased attention patterns. Unlike previous outcome-driven methods, ADAPT intervenes at the attention dynamics level, providing a more targeted solution. Experiments confirm that each component of the framework contributes to improved fidelity in image-text alignment, marking a significant advancement in mitigating hallucinations in MLLMs. By focusing on the internal behaviors of text-to-image cross-attention, this work offers a new perspective on enhancing the reliability of multimodal models. The researchers have made their code publicly available, facilitating further exploration and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose Triospect, a three-dimensional statistical framework for robust AI-generated text detection, improving detection rates against 17 attacks across 12 domains and 17 source models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Triospect, a three-dimensional statistical framework designed to improve the detection of AI-generated text, particularly against various manipulation attacks. By analyzing content, core ideas, and stylistic elements, Triospect enhances robustness across 17 different attacks, 12 domains, and 17 source models, significantly outperforming existing detection baselines. Testing on two benchmarks, including the Humanize-16K and adversarial RAID datasets, showed that Triospect increased detection accuracy by up to 22.3% in AUROC and 22% in true positive rate at a low false positive rate. This approach represents a novel statistical method to strengthen AI-generated text detection reliability, and the researchers have made their data and code publicly available for further study and development.

item.title: Researchers propose Training-Free Gated Reranking to reduce computational costs by up to 80% and improve few-shot learning performance by up to 2% across 8 LLMs and multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Training-Free Gated Reranking, a method that selectively applies reranking to few-shot learning examples based on model uncertainty. This approach challenges the common assumption that reranking always enhances performance, showing that it can sometimes degrade results. Experiments involving eight large language models across multiple natural language understanding and machine translation datasets demonstrated that this method reduces computational costs by 15% to 80% while improving average performance by up to 2%. The study highlights that higher computational expense does not necessarily lead to better outcomes and that reranking is most effective when focused on instances where the model exhibits high uncertainty. This targeted strategy offers a more efficient and potentially more accurate approach to few-shot learning tasks.

item.title: Researchers probe autonomous driving policies to link internal prediction errors with ego vehicle planning, revealing limitations in near-collision predictions and improvements from correcting mistakes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated autonomous driving policies to understand how internal prediction errors affect the planning of the ego vehicle. Their study reveals that while driving policies perform well in typical scenarios, they often fail to predict the movements of surrounding vehicles accurately during near-collision events, which limits the effectiveness of the vehicle's planning. By probing these policies through imitation learning and reinforcement learning models, the researchers identified when predictive and planning capabilities emerge or fail. The study used large datasets and simulation training to assess whether improvements in driving policies stem from better prediction and planning or simply from more effective heuristics. Targeted interventions demonstrated that correcting prediction mistakes leads to safer trajectory planning for the ego vehicle. This work highlights the importance of accurate prediction in autonomous driving and suggests that enhancing these internal signals can improve overall safety.

item.title: Researchers introduce SkillSpotter, a pose-aware multi-view model that improves skilled action detection and grading in ego-exo videos, boosting mAP by 76% and accuracy on Ego-Exo4D and HoloAssist datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SkillSpotter, a pose-aware multi-view model designed to improve the detection and grading of skilled actions in ego-exo video settings. This system addresses the challenge of not only identifying what actions a person performs but also assessing how well they execute them, which is crucial for applications like real-time coaching in sports, cooking, or music. SkillSpotter enhances performance by integrating adaptive temporal suppression, gated 3D body pose fusion, and bidirectional cross-view attention, resulting in a 76% increase in mean average precision and improved accuracy on the Ego-Exo4D and HoloAssist datasets compared to existing methods. The model builds on seven state-of-the-art temporal action detection architectures, extending evaluation protocols to separate detection from grading tasks. SkillSpotter's modules also demonstrate transferability to other temporal action detection models, showing consistent gains and generalizing beyond the initial datasets. The approach leverages body kinematics alongside visual features to better capture the nuances of skilled actions, effectively combining first-person and external camera views for comprehensive analysis.

item.title: Researchers propose UniSAE, a unified speech editing framework enabling composable speaker, emotion, and content modifications from sub-phoneme to word level using discrete phonetic posteriorgram modeling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed UniSAE, a unified speech editing framework that enables flexible modifications of speaker, emotion, and content attributes within a single system. Unlike existing methods that focus mainly on word-level content changes and treat speaker and emotion editing separately, UniSAE supports composable edits from sub-phoneme to word level by using a Discrete Phonetic PosteriorGram (DPPG) representation. This approach breaks down speech content into discrete tokens capturing phoneme identity, pronunciation variants, and duration, allowing precise and granular editing. The framework employs an autoregressive content transformer to predict edited DPPG sequences for higher-level content changes, while a diffusion-based acoustic decoder synthesizes the final speech conditioned on disentangled speaker and emotion features. Experimental results demonstrate that UniSAE effectively controls speaker and emotion attributes, supports multi-level content editing, and enables joint modification of all three attributes, offering a versatile tool for advanced speech editing applications.

item.title: Researchers propose PruneGround, a plug-and-play spatial pruning framework for 3D visual grounding that reduces computation and improves accuracy on major point cloud benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PruneGround, a plug-and-play framework designed to improve 3D Visual Grounding (3DVG) by focusing on relevant spatial regions within 3D scenes based on natural language descriptions. This approach reduces computational costs and enhances accuracy by pruning irrelevant areas, simplifying complex expressions, and aligning point cloud data with linguistic cues using a specialized language model. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on major point cloud benchmarks, including ScanRefer and Nr3D/Sr3D datasets. PruneGround incorporates three main components: Language-Guided Spatial Pruning (LGSP) to narrow down search areas using a frozen Vision Language Model, MultiView-Conditioned Description Reformulation (MCDR) to break down complex language into simpler spatial relations, and LLM-Grounder, which adapts a detection-pretrained spatial language model for grounding tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness across multiple challenging 3DVG settings, with code and models made publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce PPT-Eval, a benchmark of 120 PowerPoint tasks with a rubric-based evaluation framework showing current AI agents like Claude-4.5-Opus achieve only 45% success [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PPT-Eval, a new benchmark consisting of 120 PowerPoint tasks designed to evaluate AI agents' ability to create and edit presentations. The benchmark covers a range of content creation and editing scenarios and includes a rubric-based evaluation framework that awards partial credit and provides detailed feedback, addressing the complexity and multimodal nature of these tasks. Despite advances, leading AI models like Claude-4.5-Opus achieve only a 45% success rate, highlighting ongoing challenges in this domain. The evaluation framework developed for PPT-Eval incorporates task-specific rubrics that penalize unnecessary changes and poor aesthetics while rewarding intermediate progress, resulting in a strong correlation with human judgments. This nuanced approach captures partial successes better than binary metrics, reflecting the varied valid solutions possible in PowerPoint tasks. The benchmark is publicly available for further research and development in improving AI performance on real-world computer-use tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose AETDICE, an offline reinforcement learning algorithm unifying nonlinear multi-objective RL optimization through the Aggregation-Expectation-Transformation framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced AETDICE, a new offline reinforcement learning algorithm designed to optimize nonlinear preferences in multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL). This approach unifies two previously separate paradigms-Scalarized Expected Return (SER) and Expected Scalarized Return (ESR)-through the Aggregation-Expectation-Transformation (AET) framework, which decomposes scalarization into three components to provide a comprehensive foundation for nonlinear MORL. AETDICE leverages DICE-style density-ratio estimation within an augmented state space, enabling effective sample-based optimization from static datasets. This method addresses longstanding challenges in nonlinear MORL by capturing the trade-offs inherent in the AET framework, which prior techniques have been unable to resolve.

item.title: Researchers introduce Bayesian in-context experimenters using transformers to efficiently estimate average treatment effects with adaptive allocation and smoothness adaptation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Bayesian in-context experimenters using transformer models to improve the efficiency of estimating average treatment effects (ATE) in adaptive experiments. These transformers are trained to mimic a Bayesian posterior Neyman teacher, which updates beliefs about potential outcomes based on experimental history to assign treatment probabilities. This approach converges to the optimal oracle design, enhancing statistical efficiency and valid inference in ATE estimation. The method employs attention mechanisms and projected gradient descent to replicate Bayesian updating for Gaussian-series priors. To handle unknown outcome smoothness, the researchers use a mixture-of-experts transformer that adapts by focusing on near-optimal experts based on smoothness classes. The policy can be learned through supervised pretraining and empirical risk minimization, with experiments demonstrating accurate imitation of the teacher, adaptive allocation, and improved precision compared to baseline methods.

item.title: Researchers propose Multi-View Gated Graph Attention Network using speech graphs for Alzheimer's detection, achieving 90% accuracy on ADReSSo dataset with code publicly available [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Multi-View Gated Graph Attention Network to detect Alzheimer's Disease using spontaneous speech. The model transcribes audio with Automatic Speech Recognition to create semantic, dependency, and co-occurrence graphs, capturing speech characteristics through a "content-structure-flow" framework. It incorporates Pointwise Mutual Information from a normative corpus to assess narrative coherence and linguistic deviations, and uses an adaptive gated fusion mechanism to handle clinical heterogeneity. Tested on the ADReSSo dataset, the approach achieved 90% accuracy, with ablation studies highlighting the importance of the PMI-based graph and heterogeneity-aware gating for robust classification. The source code for this method is publicly available.

item.title: Researchers introduce PSALM framework to evaluate stylistic appropriation and copyright infringement risks in large language models under EU law, revealing limitations of current safeguards [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PSALM, a framework designed to evaluate the risks of stylistic appropriation and copyright infringement by large language models (LLMs) under European Union law. Unlike existing safeguards that focus mainly on verbatim copying, PSALM assesses broader aspects such as writing style, narrative structure, and creative elements, aligning with the EU's standard of substantial similarity. The framework was applied to Llama 3.2 models fine-tuned on historical Dutch literature, revealing that fine-tuning leads to systematic stylistic appropriation beyond literal memorization, and that current unlearning techniques reduce but do not eliminate these patterns. PSALM uses ten evaluators to measure computational overlap, stylistic and content dimensions, and statutory exceptions like parody and quotation. The study found that instruction-tuned models already exhibit baseline stylistic similarities before exposure to specific corpora, and that fine-tuning amplifies these effects across multiple infringement-relevant dimensions. These findings highlight a significant gap in current copyright compliance methods, which focus narrowly on literal copying and overlook broader stylistic risks. The framework offers a foundation for legally informed, auditable compliance evaluation, though the connection between automated similarity scores and legal infringement requires further validation by experts. This work bridges the gap between qualitative legal standards and quantitative technical measures, underscoring fundamental challenges at the intersection of generative AI and EU intellectual property law.

item.title: Researchers introduce TDGT, a web-based toolkit for synthetic tabular data generation using adaptive GPU-accelerated Bayesian mixture models and latent-space generative modeling with multi-metric fidelity assessment [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TDGT (Tabular Data Generation Toolkit), a web-based platform designed to generate synthetic tabular data with high fidelity while preserving privacy. TDGT features the Adaptive Bayesian Mixture Synthesizer (ABMS), which automatically optimizes the number of mixture components without manual tuning, and a hybrid model called VAE-ABMS that combines variational autoencoders with adaptive Bayesian mixtures to capture complex data distributions. The toolkit also includes a GPU-accelerated version for large datasets and evaluates synthetic data quality using multiple statistical metrics alongside privacy risk assessments. The toolkit supports real-time data streaming and interactive visualizations, making it accessible for users across various domains such as healthcare, socioeconomic modeling, and cybersecurity. Evaluations demonstrate that TDGT consistently produces statistically coherent synthetic data across diverse feature types and scales, addressing the growing need for privacy-preserving data sharing in AI workflows.

item.title: Researchers develop CSO-LLM, a class subspace orthogonalization method for post-training backdoor detection and trigger inversion in large language models across multiple architectures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CSO-LLM, a novel method called class subspace orthogonalization, to detect and invert backdoor triggers in large language models (LLMs) after training. This approach addresses challenges unique to LLMs, such as the vast discrete input space and the difficulty of blacklisting tokens associated with targeted attack responses. CSO enhances the sensitivity and specificity of backdoor detection by implicitly penalizing tokens that align with the target class of an attack, improving detection accuracy without requiring comprehensive blacklists. The method includes two complementary techniques: one that optimizes continuously in token embedding space and another that performs greedy token selection in discrete space. Tested across multiple LLM architectures and classification tasks, CSO-LLM demonstrated strong performance in both detecting backdoors and accurately recovering the original triggers, offering a robust framework for securing LLMs against post-training backdoor attacks.

item.title: Researchers demonstrate AI-assisted visual analytics prototyping using Artifact-Transform Workflow Language, reducing development time from months to an afternoon [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that using the Artifact-Transform Workflow Language (ATWL) combined with an AI assistant can significantly accelerate the prototyping of visual analytics ideas, reducing the process from months to just an afternoon. This approach was applied to a new method involving relaxing the Pareto frontier and grouping options into recurring types, resulting in a consistent workflow within minutes and a functional prototype in a few hours. The study highlights three key findings: the importance of the scaffold provided by ATWL, the necessity of expert knowledge to achieve high-quality results beyond the initial AI-generated prototype, and the impact of how the scaffold is used. Controlled experiments showed that providing both a language definition and example library simultaneously can hinder creativity, and that scaffolds are most effective when introduced after an initial unconstrained design phase. The researchers suggest developing a typology of human knowledge injection that is both human-editable and machine-accessible to further enhance this process.

item.title: Researchers use sparse autoencoders to resolve superposition in AI models trained on 100,000 patient-derived neuronal images, enabling interpretable latent representations and cross-modal alignment with single-cell RNA sequencing data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to address the issue of superposition in neural networks trained on over 100,000 multiplexed images of patient-derived neurons from Parkinson's disease and healthy controls. This approach improves interpretability by recovering the geometric fidelity of latent representations, which are then analyzed similarly to single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. The team introduced GW-map, a technique that aligns these image-based representations with authentic scRNA-seq data using Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport, enabling the reconstruction of neuronal pathology pathways without relying on spatial transcriptomics. The study highlights how superposition distorts the geometry of latent spaces in AI models and demonstrates that SAEs can effectively purify these representations. By treating the purified latent vectors as single-cell state vectors, the researchers adapted scRNA-seq analytical methods to image data, facilitating cross-modal alignment. This work establishes a scalable foundation for spatial biology and offers new tools for interpreting complex biological data through AI. The associated code has been made publicly available for further research and application.

item.title: Researchers introduce Mixture-of-Control, a state-aware fine-tuning framework for transformers that enables efficient cross-block communication and outperforms existing state-based methods with comparable memory and computational efficiency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Mixture-of-Control (MoC), a novel fine-tuning framework for transformer models that enhances cross-block communication by integrating local and global control signals. Unlike traditional state-based fine-tuning methods that update controls only within individual blocks, MoC treats block-wise control states as experts in a sparse mixture-of-experts process, enabling efficient information exchange across transformer blocks. This approach maintains comparable memory and computational efficiency while improving representational adaptation. MoC addresses the limitations of existing state-based methods, which often restrict inter-block communication or incur significant computational overhead when enabling it. Empirical evaluations across various transformer benchmarks demonstrate that MoC outperforms current state-based fine-tuning techniques, offering a more effective and efficient solution for adapting transformer-based models.

item.title: Researchers propose Visual Semantic Entropy to measure visual ambiguity in vision-language models, outperforming existing uncertainty estimation methods across five VQA benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Visual Semantic Entropy (VSE), a new method to measure visual ambiguity in vision-language models (VLMs). Unlike previous entropy-based approaches that rely on output diversity and can underestimate uncertainty due to overconfident visual embeddings, VSE perturbs only the image input while keeping the text query fixed. This approach clusters generated answers into semantic prototypes and calculates uncertainty based on their dispersion, effectively capturing visual ambiguity. The team evaluated VSE across five modern vision-language models and five diverse visual question answering (VQA) benchmarks. Their results show that VSE outperforms existing uncertainty estimation methods, which often reflect sensitivity to textual changes rather than true visual ambiguity. This establishes VSE as a state-of-the-art technique for assessing uncertainty in VLMs, improving the reliability of their predictions on ambiguous visual inputs.

item.title: Team MKC proposes an LLM-based pipeline for analyzing mental health changes through social media timeline dynamics at CLPsych 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Team MKC has developed a pipeline using Large Language Models (LLMs) to analyze mental health changes by examining the sequence of user posts on social media. Presented at the CLPsych 2026 shared task, this approach integrates both post-level evaluation and user-level temporal modeling to provide a comprehensive assessment of psychological well-being. This work addresses the growing need for scalable computational tools to support early detection and ongoing monitoring of mental health, especially given the increasing prevalence of mental health disorders and limited access to professional care. By leveraging domain-specific datasets, the pipeline aims to enhance holistic mental health analysis through advanced AI techniques.

item.title: Researchers introduce FinPersona-Bench to measure mandate salience decay in autonomous financial agents using 18 LLMs across simulated market scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed FinPersona-Bench, a simulation benchmark designed to measure Mandate Salience Decay (MSD) in autonomous financial agents powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). MSD refers to the gradual loss of influence of explicit behavioral mandates, such as capital preservation or avoiding speculative bets, as market context accumulates over time. The benchmark evaluates 18 leading LLMs across simulated market scenarios that separate observable prices from hidden fundamental values, testing agents' behaviors in calm markets, crashes, and speculative bubbles. The study assigns each LLM one of three behavioral profiles ranging from conservative to aggressive and finds that MSD increases over time and varies by model. In crash scenarios, agents receiving periodic mandate re-grounding show a behavioral gap 4.4 times larger than static agents by the simulation's end. While re-grounding improves performance for conservative agents in low-signal markets, it can worsen outcomes for aggressive agents, indicating that effective long-term deployment requires selective, mandate-aware adjustments tailored to agent profiles and market conditions.

item.title: Researchers propose SAIL-RevKL algorithm with reverse KL divergence penalty, proving global convergence and improved performance on LLM alignment and MuJoCo benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SAIL-RevKL, a new algorithm that enhances the Self-Improving Alignment (SAIL) method by incorporating a reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence penalty to address optimization challenges. This modification improves the algorithm's convergence properties, with the team proving that the regularized objective satisfies the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, ensuring global convergence with near-linear sample complexity. Empirical tests show that SAIL-RevKL outperforms the original SAIL on both large language model alignment tasks and MuJoCo benchmarks. The original SAIL algorithm tackled distribution shifts by simplifying a bilevel problem into a single-level approach but lacked formal convergence guarantees due to the non-strongly concave nature of its objective function. By adding the reverse KL divergence penalty, SAIL-RevKL improves the optimization landscape, enabling theoretical analysis and practical stability. This advancement offers a more reliable and efficient method for online alignment in machine learning applications.

item.title: Researchers find high-fidelity room-acoustic simulations reduce word error rate by up to 38% in multichannel speech enhancement training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that using high-fidelity room-acoustic simulations to augment training data significantly improves multichannel speech enhancement performance. By training the SpatialNet model on datasets generated with advanced acoustic modeling techniques, including a hybrid of wave-based and geometrical acoustics simulations, they achieved up to a 38% relative reduction in median word error rate compared to models trained on lower-fidelity geometrical acoustics data. The study involved comparing different simulation methods and evaluating the resulting models on measured speech data. The findings highlight that more physically accurate room-acoustic simulations provide better training data for deep-learning-based speech enhancement, leading to more effective noise reduction and clearer speech recognition in multichannel audio systems.

item.title: Researchers propose Physics-aware Neural Operator Transformer for real-time temperature field reconstruction of tungsten monoblock divertor on EAST fusion device [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a Physics-aware Neural Operator Transformer (PNOT) to enable real-time reconstruction of the temperature field in the tungsten monoblock divertor of the EAST fusion device. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional numerical methods like the Finite Element Method, which are too computationally intensive for real-time use. PNOT models boundary heat-flux relations as a structured graph and uses graph attention mechanisms to capture spatial physical dependencies, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of temperature field predictions. The model incorporates a physics-aware neural operator module that aggregates query points with similar physical conditions and simulates heat diffusion, supported by a gradient-constrained Sobolev regularization loss to maintain consistency between function values and their derivatives. Experimental results demonstrate that these physics-based constraints improve prediction accuracy while preserving physical consistency. The researchers plan to release the source code to facilitate further development and application in fusion device control.

item.title: Researchers find optimiser choice drives a 7x variation in emergent misalignment in LLM fine-tuning, with spectral regularisation mitigating effects of EM-prone optimisers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified that the choice of optimiser significantly influences emergent misalignment (EM) in large language model (LLM) fine-tuning, causing up to a sevenfold variation in misalignment rates. EM occurs when fine-tuning on a narrowly misaligned task leads to broadly misaligned behavior on unrelated prompts. Their study across multiple Qwen3 models, optimisers, datasets, and batch sizes found that optimiser choice outweighs model size in affecting EM severity, with model scale and family having negligible impact when using the Adam optimiser. The team analyzed training dynamics and found that different optimisers follow distinct trajectories in loss-alignment space, with the optimiser becoming a stronger predictor of alignment than training loss after extensive training. The adaptive optimiser Muon was noted for preserving alignment best by implicitly regularizing the singular value distribution of the LoRA adapter. Introducing a spectral regularisation loss term to encourage a flatter singular value spectrum substantially improved alignment for EM-prone optimisers like Adam and Lion, without compromising training loss. These findings highlight optimiser choice as a key factor in EM severity and demonstrate that spectral regularisation can effectively mitigate the negative effects of certain adaptive optimisers, offering a promising approach to improving alignment in LLM fine-tuning.

item.title: Researchers propose uncertainty-guided synthetic data augmentation using diffusion models to improve semantic segmentation on Cityscapes, UAVID, and BDD100K datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an uncertainty-guided synthetic data augmentation method using diffusion models to enhance semantic segmentation performance on datasets such as Cityscapes, UAVID, and BDD100K. This approach targets uncertain semantic regions identified by a baseline segmenter's predictive entropy and inpaints only the surrounding visual context, preserving label accuracy and focusing training on challenging areas without relying on external models or broad heuristics. The method yields significant improvements in mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), especially for rare and difficult classes like buses, trains, and aerial-view cars. The technique involves fine-tuning the segmentation model using synthetic data where the loss is computed solely over the original uncertain pixels, excluding the inpainted regions. This strategy efficiently maximizes the informativeness of each synthetic sample by presenting uncertain regions in novel contexts while maintaining label validity. The researchers provide code to facilitate adoption and demonstrate that uncertainty-guided context augmentation is an effective tool for improving segmentation on complex and diverse datasets.

item.title: Researchers propose ECHO, a selective turn-memory framework for agentic reinforcement learning that improves accuracy and traceable learning by compressing and reconstructing environment turns [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ECHO, a selective turn-memory framework designed to enhance agentic reinforcement learning for long-horizon language tasks. ECHO addresses limitations in existing context-management methods by compressing each environment turn into compact memory records and reconstructing policy contexts through selective retrieval. This approach improves accuracy and enables traceable learning by linking policy updates directly to the evidence supporting successful outcomes. ECHO outperforms previous methods on the BrowseComp-Plus benchmark, achieving 43.4% held-out accuracy compared to 28.9% for GRPO and 36.1% for the rolling-summary baseline SUPO, while using fewer turns and less trajectory data. Additionally, the trained policy demonstrates improved zero-shot generalization across various tasks, including multi-objective question answering, code generation, and deep information-seeking, on both dense and mixture-of-experts model backbones.

item.title: Researchers introduce AD-CERT, combining adversarial distillation with Interval Bound Propagation to improve certified robustness and achieve state-of-the-art performance on robustness benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AD-CERT, a new certified training method that combines adversarial distillation with Interval Bound Propagation (IBP) to enhance the certified robustness of neural networks. This approach leverages adversarial information distilled from a robust teacher model at the logit level, serving as an effective lower bound surrogate for certified training. AD-CERT achieves state-of-the-art performance on several robustness benchmarks, improving the balance between standard accuracy and certified robustness compared to previous methods. Traditional certified training methods often sacrifice standard accuracy to ensure formal verification against adversarial perturbations, while adversarial training improves empirical robustness but is harder to certify. AD-CERT addresses this trade-off by integrating adversarial distillation with an IBP upper bound, effectively interpolating between lower and upper bounds of worst-case loss. The study also shows that logit-level adversarial distillation outperforms robust feature-space distillation by up to 5.40 percentage points in certified accuracy, marking a significant advancement in certified robustness training techniques.

item.title: Researchers introduce Histogram-constrained Image Generation, a diffusion model control method enforcing user-specified distributional constraints via optimal transport for precise image generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Histogram-constrained Image Generation (HIG), a new method for controlling diffusion models in image generation by enforcing user-defined distributional constraints such as color histograms or latent token distributions. This approach uses optimal transport theory to guide the diffusion process, ensuring precise alignment with the specified histogram during sampling. HIG offers a control granularity between global semantic guidance and detailed local conditioning, addressing challenges in balancing overall coherence with local accuracy in generated images. The method demonstrates versatility across various applications, including constrained image generation and high-capacity information embedding through histogram-level encoding. HIG is compatible with existing control mechanisms, enabling hybrid strategies for more flexible and interpretable control over image generation. This advancement broadens the toolkit for controllable generative modeling, enhancing the ability to produce images that meet specific distributional criteria.

item.title: Researchers propose a residual-overlap stopping rule for feature ranking truncation to select subsets with calibrated risk bounds, validated on high-dimensional genomic data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new stopping rule for feature ranking truncation in supervised feature selection, addressing the challenge of determining when to stop selecting features based on accumulated class-separation evidence. Their method uses the Bhattacharyya coefficient to measure marginal separation between class-conditional distributions and selects a global subset by retaining the shortest prefix of a ranking whose residual product overlap falls below a set threshold for all relevant class contrasts. This approach provides explicit risk-calibrated stopping criteria, moving beyond arbitrary or empirical thresholds commonly used in practice. The team derived Bayes-risk bounds for both binary and multiclass cases and calibrated the residual-overlap threshold to target specific risk levels. Empirical tests on high-dimensional genomic datasets demonstrated that the method can reduce tens of thousands of variables to a few dozen while maintaining predictive performance comparable to using all features. Because the stopping rule relies only on one-dimensional marginal overlap estimates and scans a precomputed ranking, it is particularly suited for very high-dimensional settings where exhaustive subset search is impractical and interpretable feature selection is critical.

item.title: Researchers propose ShopX, a foundation model unifying intent understanding and item-space operations for agentic shopping, improving multi-turn fulfillment in Taobao production logs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ShopX, a foundation model designed to unify intent understanding and item-space operations for agentic shopping, enhancing multi-turn fulfillment processes. ShopX integrates intent comprehension, execution planning, and semantic ID-based item operations into a single model, addressing limitations in current systems that separate language understanding from item fulfillment. The model is deployed within a framework that supports context access, catalog grounding, and state management, enabling more seamless and flexible shopping interactions. ShopX introduces semantically recoverable, LLM-operable semantic IDs (SIDs) and a training approach that equips a general large language model to handle complex, multi-turn item-space fulfillment while maintaining instruction-following capabilities. Evaluations using anonymized Taobao production logs demonstrate that ShopX's model-native fulfillment approach outperforms traditional tool-mediated systems, particularly in handling complex or ambiguous shopping requests, reducing inefficiencies caused by hand-offs between language understanding and item execution.

item.title: Researchers release RCT, a robot-collected touch-vision-language dataset with 29,279 tactile frames on 122 materials to study tactile generalization and held-out material evaluation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced RCT (Robotic Contact Tactile), a comprehensive dataset designed to advance robotic tactile perception by enabling generalization to unseen materials. The dataset includes 29,279 tactile frames collected from robot presses on 122 industrial materials across seven categories, captured using three DIGIT sensors at various contact points. RCT preserves each press as a contact sequence, allowing for rigorous evaluation of tactile models on held-out materials, categories, sensors, and contact positions, highlighting challenges in generalizing tactile representations beyond training data. The study reveals that frames within a single press are highly correlated, and traditional random frame splits can lead to near-duplicate data in both training and testing sets, inflating performance metrics. When contact-sequence overlap is removed, the accuracy of tactile-to-text retrieval drops significantly, and further exclusion of materials during training causes a sharp decline in performance. The dataset supports improved contrastive training methods and enhances category recognition on unseen materials, emphasizing the importance of contact-sequence-aware evaluation for reproducible and realistic assessment of robotic tactile perception. The RCT dataset is publicly available for research use.

item.title: Researchers evaluate large language models for cross-lingual relation extraction on Romanian, finding fine-tuned QLoRA improves F1 by 22 points but smaller encoders perform comparably [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored cross-lingual relation extraction (RE) for Romanian by translating an English benchmark dataset and evaluating large language models (LLMs) alongside smaller encoder models. They tested the Gemma 4 31B model in zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned (QLoRA) settings, comparing it to four encoder baselines ranging from 125M to 560M parameters. Fine-tuning with QLoRA significantly improved performance, boosting the macro F1 score by over 22 points and narrowing the performance gap between English and Romanian. Despite the large model's gains, smaller encoder models performed comparably on Romanian, with the 125M-parameter Romanian BERT matching the multilingual XLM-R at 278M parameters. This suggests that deploying the large 31B model for single-task RE in Romanian may not be efficient when computational resources are limited. The researchers have made the translated dataset, evaluation code, and trained models publicly available to support further work in this area.

item.title: Researchers find vision-language models overestimate shared understanding in dialogue by conflating potential and established common ground using map content [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that some vision-language models (VLMs) tend to overestimate mutual understanding in collaborative dialogues by confusing potential shared knowledge with what has actually been established. Their study, based on 13,077 annotated reference expressions from HCRC MapTask dialogues, shows that while providing authentic map images improves model performance, it also leads to an over-prediction of alignment between dialogue participants. This bias appears driven by task-relevant map content rather than the visual presentation itself, as textual descriptions of the same maps produce similar effects. The analysis revealed that models often rely on static referential cues from the maps instead of tracking how mutual understanding develops through dialogue history. This pattern was most evident in the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct model and observed to varying degrees in other models across different architectures. The findings highlight a tendency in these models to treat map content as direct evidence of shared understanding, conflating what could be shared with what is actually shared in dialogue.

item.title: Researchers introduce FedXDS, a federated learning method using explainable AI to guide selective data sharing and mitigate client data heterogeneity with privacy guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed FedXDS, a novel federated learning approach that leverages explainable AI (XAI) to address the challenge of client data heterogeneity while maintaining privacy. FedXDS uses feature attribution techniques to identify and selectively share relevant data elements among clients, improving model performance without exposing raw data. This method incorporates metric privacy to ensure formal privacy guarantees and demonstrates higher accuracy and faster convergence compared to existing methods across various client and heterogeneity scenarios. By employing propagation-based attribution, FedXDS identifies task-relevant features through a single backward pass, enabling efficient and targeted data sharing that aligns client contributions. The approach also provides theoretical privacy assurances and shows robustness against membership inference and feature inversion attacks, making it a promising solution for collaborative learning in privacy-sensitive environments. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and validation.

item.title: Researchers present CHERRY techniques for compute-efficient language models including selective supervision, depth compression with recurrent recovery, and fusion of compressed experts, validated on a 1.8B-parameter Korean model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CHERRY, a set of three techniques aimed at improving the compute efficiency of language models. These include Selective Ground Truth Token Training (SGT), which focuses supervision on the 15% of output tokens carrying semantic content while still enhancing the remaining tokens through gradient coupling; depth compression with recurrent recovery, which reduces a 48-layer transformer to 6 layers and restores performance via learned recurrent unrolling; and the fusion of compressed experts, combining multiple compressed models into a Mixture of Efficient Experts (MoEE) to improve prediction accuracy. These methods were validated on CHERRY-1.8B, a Korean language foundation model developed by the researchers. The study demonstrates that SGT achieves a 4.5-fold increase in per-supervised-token efficiency, recovering about 67% of the full-sequence loss reduction from limited supervision. Depth compression reduces model parameters by 2.5 times while maintaining comparable performance to larger dense models. The MoEE approach further enhances results by leveraging multiple compressed experts. The researchers emphasize that their findings are based on one model family, Korean data, and loss-based metrics, clearly distinguishing established results from prospective claims.

item.title: Researchers propose geometry-preserving orthonormal initialization for low-rank adaptation in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, improving stability and performance over existing LoRA variants [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a geometry-preserving orthonormal initialization method for low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), addressing instability and performance issues seen in existing LoRA variants. Their theoretical analysis shows that orthonormal initialization minimizes the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning, leading to two new variants, RLPO and RLMO, which stabilize training and outperform standard LoRA on mathematical reasoning benchmarks. The study highlights that previously proposed LoRA variants like PiSSA and MiLoRA, while effective under supervised fine-tuning, can underperform and cause instability in RLVR settings. The new initialization approach preserves geometric properties of the adaptation matrices, providing a unified explanation for these differences and improving reliability in RLVR fine-tuning. The researchers have made their code and checkpoints publicly available for further exploration.

item.title: Researchers introduce MECoBench, a benchmark and evaluation platform for studying multimodal agent collaboration in embodied environments across diverse tasks and cooperation modes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MECoBench, a new benchmark and evaluation platform designed to study collaboration among multimodal large language models (MLLMs) acting as embodied agents in visually grounded environments. MECoBench covers a range of real-world tasks, cooperation structures, and collaboration modes, providing a comprehensive framework to assess how these agents work together. The study reveals that collaboration generally enhances task completion, but its effectiveness depends on balancing the benefits of cooperation with the complexity of coordination. The research highlights three key findings: communication is crucial for successful collaboration, the optimal collaboration mode varies with team size and model capabilities, and collaboration improves robustness in challenging conditions such as noisy inputs and exploration tasks. MECoBench offers a systematic approach to understanding the dynamics and limitations of multimodal embodied agent collaboration, with the code and dataset made publicly available for further research.

item.title: Researchers introduce MADreMIA, a model-agnostic framework using chained regenerations to enhance membership inference and dataset attacks across modalities without shadow model training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MADreMIA, a model-agnostic framework designed to improve membership inference attacks (MIA) and dataset inference (DI) on large generative models without the need for shadow model training. By using chained regenerations-where each output is fed back as input across multiple iterations-MADreMIA enhances the detection of memorized training data, which is crucial for privacy auditing and copyright enforcement. This approach works across various modalities and model types, including image autoregressive models, diffusion models, language models, and shows promise for audio models as well. MADreMIA leverages iterative trajectories to amplify membership signals, demonstrating that memorized samples maintain higher coherence and degrade more slowly during regeneration compared to non-member samples. This method provides richer and more sensitive signals than traditional one-shot generation attacks, enabling scalable and effective inference in white-, gray-, and black-box settings without relying on computationally expensive shadow models.

item.title: Researchers present geometric analysis showing radial suppression accelerates algorithmic generalization by reducing memorization delay in neural networks, validated on MLPs, Transformers, and nanoGPT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted a geometric analysis revealing that the delay in neural networks generalizing algorithmic training data is caused by radial inflation of hidden representations during cross-entropy optimization. They propose a radial-angular decomposition of activation dynamics and demonstrate that penalizing radial inflation leads to anisotropic, data-dependent weight regularization, suppresses radial gradient energy, and biases convergence toward flatter minima. This approach was empirically validated using a norm penalty that constrains activations to a hypersphere, significantly accelerating generalization on modular arithmetic tasks across MLPs, Transformers, and a 10-million-parameter nanoGPT model.

item.title: Researchers propose TRIAGE, a role-typed credit assignment framework for agentic reinforcement learning that improves success rates and reduces environment-facing turns across ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TRIAGE, a role-typed credit assignment framework designed to enhance agentic reinforcement learning by more accurately assigning credit to environment-facing actions such as searches, clicks, and navigation commands. Unlike standard methods that use a uniform advantage based on final outcomes, TRIAGE incorporates a semantic role axis to classify action segments into categories like decisive progress, useful exploration, or regression, allowing for more nuanced and effective credit assignment. This approach improves success rates and reduces unnecessary environment interactions across benchmarks including ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop. TRIAGE employs a structured judge to label segments and applies fixed role-conditioned rules to assign bounded process rewards, addressing the limitations of outcome-only credit assignment which can penalize useful exploration or reinforce redundant actions. The framework demonstrates optimal segment-level correction based on role labels, reducing advantage estimation error and lowering policy gradient variance. Experimental results show TRIAGE outperforms existing methods, with ablation studies highlighting the importance of role typing and reliable regression detection in driving performance gains, as well as a significant reduction in environment-facing turns during task completion.

item.title: Researchers propose AdaJEPA, an adaptive latent world model that performs test-time adaptation within model predictive control to improve planning success under distribution shifts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced AdaJEPA, an adaptive latent world model designed to improve planning success in environments with distribution shifts by performing test-time adaptation within model predictive control (MPC). Unlike traditional latent world models that remain fixed during testing, AdaJEPA updates its predictions by using observed state transitions as self-supervised signals to recalibrate the model continuously without requiring additional expert input. This approach enhances the model's ability to plan effectively from high-dimensional observations by adjusting to new conditions in real time. AdaJEPA operates by planning and executing an initial set of actions, then using the resulting state transitions to perform gradient-based updates before replanning. This closed-loop adaptation allows the model to maintain accuracy and robustness across various goal-reaching tasks, significantly increasing planning success with minimal computational overhead, often requiring just one gradient step per replanning cycle.

item.title: Researchers introduce Freeform Preference Learning to train robotic manipulation policies using natural-language human preferences, improving performance by 38 percentage points across real and simulated tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Freeform Preference Learning (FPL), a novel method for training robotic manipulation policies using natural-language human preferences. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on binary comparisons of trajectories, FPL allows annotators to specify preference axes such as speed, safety, or carefulness and provide pairwise preferences along these dimensions. This approach enables the learning of a language-conditioned reward model that guides policy optimization across multiple human-defined criteria, resulting in a 38 percentage point improvement over existing sparse-reward and binary-preference methods in both real-world and simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks. FPL not only enhances performance but also generates dense progress signals without requiring explicit subtask segmentation. It demonstrates compositional behavior beyond the training data and allows users to adjust the robot's behavior at test time without retraining. This flexibility and improved learning signal represent significant advances in autonomous robot policy development for complex manipulation tasks.

item.title: Researchers systematically evaluate data referencing errors in large language models on table tasks and improve accuracy by up to 12% using a 4B-parameter critic model for error detection and inference assistance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted the first systematic evaluation of data referencing errors (DREs) in large language models (LLMs) when performing table-related tasks. These errors, which involve incorrectly citing or omitting table values, affect models ranging from 1.7 billion to 20 billion parameters and undermine the accuracy and reliability of intermediate reasoning steps despite the models' understanding of table structures. The study demonstrates that integrating a data referencing critic can improve answer accuracy by up to 12% through methods like critic-based filtering and rejection sampling. The team developed a lightweight 4-billion-parameter critic model that detects DREs with an average F1 score of 78.2%, effectively identifying errors both within and outside the training distribution. This critic model also assists larger models during inference, enhancing their performance on table tasks by reducing referencing mistakes.

item.title: Researchers propose reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback to improve large language models' uncertainty calibration and self-assessment accuracy, outperforming standard methods by up to 63% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a novel approach called reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback (RLMF) to enhance large language models' (LLMs) ability to accurately assess and express their own uncertainty. This method improves the calibration of models' confidence scores by refining completion rankings based on the quality of their self-judgments, addressing common issues such as overconfidence and misrepresentation of uncertainty that undermine LLM reliability. Experiments demonstrate that RLMF outperforms standard reinforcement learning techniques by up to 63%, achieving state-of-the-art results in faithful calibration while maintaining task accuracy. The approach involves a two-stage process: first, calibrating the faithfulness of self-reported confidence scores using metacognitive feedback, and second, translating these calibrated scores into natural, context-sensitive linguistic uncertainty through targeted output editing. Additionally, metacognitive data selection leverages self-assessments to identify valuable training examples, surpassing traditional active learning methods. This work highlights metacognitive performance as an effective reinforcement learning signal, offering a promising direction for improving LLM metacognition, trustworthiness, and alignment with human expectations.

item.title: Researchers analyze horizontal and vertical deductive reasoning mechanisms in small transformer language models using Chain-of-Thought supervision on synthetic logic tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers investigated how small transformer-based language models perform deductive reasoning by distinguishing between horizontal reasoning, which generates intermediate steps autoregressively, and vertical reasoning, where inference occurs implicitly across layers before output. Using synthetic tasks involving symbolic logic chains and binary tree navigation, they found that Chain-of-Thought supervision helps models learn rule-based inference rather than relying on statistical shortcuts. In horizontal reasoning, shallow attention models developed interpretable mechanisms for rule completion and chaining, while vertical reasoning benefited from Chain-of-Thought as a form of curriculum learning to acquire complex reasoning patterns. The study introduced a truncated pseudoinverse method to decode information in model components and showed that without Chain-of-Thought supervision, models tend to memorize or exploit dataset biases. These findings provide insight into how transformers implement deductive logic and suggest that Chain-of-Thought plays different roles in horizontal versus vertical reasoning processes.

item.title: Researchers introduce ReplicatorBench, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on replicability of social and behavioral science claims across data retrieval, experiment design, and result interpretation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ReplicatorBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents on their ability to replicate social and behavioral science claims. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus mainly on reproducing results with available code and data, ReplicatorBench assesses AI agents across the full replication process, including data retrieval, experiment design, and result interpretation, using both replicable and non-replicable human-verified research claims. To establish a baseline, the team developed ReplicatorAgent, an AI framework equipped with tools such as web search and sandboxed environment interaction to perform tasks in ReplicatorBench. Evaluations across multiple LLMs showed that while these agents can effectively design and execute computational experiments, they face challenges in retrieving new data necessary for replication. The benchmark and associated resources are publicly available to support further research in automated scientific replication.

item.title: Researchers propose a multi-dimensional behavioral framework to measure reasoning quality in LLMs across six dimensions, revealing insights beyond accuracy on seven models and four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a multi-dimensional behavioral framework to evaluate the reasoning quality of large language models (LLMs) beyond just final-answer accuracy. The framework assesses six dimensions-Correctness, Consistency, Robustness, Logical Coherence, Efficiency, and Stability-across seven LLMs and four benchmarks, revealing insights that accuracy alone cannot capture. For example, logical coherence was found to be independent of correctness, indicating that correct answers can result from incoherent reasoning, and the framework identified ranking reversals among models that single-metric evaluations missed. Extensive testing showed that most dimensions are independent, supporting their use as distinct measures of reasoning quality. The framework's detailed profiles can help identify models that might fail accountability audits despite correct answers, prevent errors in model ranking caused by relying solely on accuracy, and ensure comprehensive evaluation by capturing multiple independent signals. This approach offers a more nuanced understanding of LLM reasoning capabilities and supports better-informed deployment decisions.

item.title: Researchers find Bellman optimality in Markov decision processes with catastrophic states produces prospect-theory-like behavior including S-shaped value functions and loss aversion without utility curvature [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that standard Bellman optimality in Markov decision processes (MDPs) with absorbing catastrophic states can produce behaviors similar to those described by prospect theory, even when agents are risk-neutral and rewards are linear. This includes S-shaped value functions, loss aversion, and policy reversals depending on the regime, without requiring utility curvature or probability weighting. The study demonstrates that optimal policies tend to be risk-averse near catastrophic states in growth scenarios and risk-seeking in decline scenarios, reflecting prospect-theory-like decision patterns. The team derived a closed-form expression for the asymptotic loss-aversion coefficient, which depends on win probability, payoff asymmetry, and discount factor, closely matching numerical results. These phenomena persist under various conditions, including model-free Q-learning and stochastic transitions with different noise distributions. The findings suggest that the presence of absorbing failure states alone can structurally induce prospect-theory-like behavior under optimal control in MDPs.

item.title: Researchers find low-bit quantization in reasoning models preserves accuracy but increases reasoning-token usage, causing hidden compute costs and longer reasoning chains across benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that low-bit post-training quantization of reasoning models, such as INT4 and INT3, can maintain accuracy but leads to longer chains of thought during reasoning tasks. This increase in reasoning-token usage offsets the expected speedup from quantization, introducing hidden compute costs despite preserved final-answer accuracy. The study covers various benchmarks including mathematical reasoning, code generation, scientific question answering, and agentic tool use. The team introduced the CoT Token Inflation Ratio to quantify the increase in reasoning length between quantized and full-precision models. They observed that token inflation is linked to behavioral changes in the reasoning process, such as more intermediate steps and greater semantic repetition, which result in measurable real-world performance penalties. Mitigation strategies like prompting and decoding-time sampling showed inconsistent results, while quantization-aware training demonstrated better potential in reducing both accuracy loss and token inflation. These findings suggest that evaluations of quantized reasoning models should report reasoning-token usage alongside accuracy to fully capture the trade-offs involved. This insight highlights the need for more nuanced metrics when assessing the efficiency and effectiveness of quantized language models in reasoning tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose using Behavioral Foundation Models for online exploration and zero-shot transfer in reinforcement learning, framing it as a bandit problem with policy recommendations and reward feedback [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have proposed a new approach to zero-shot transfer in reinforcement learning (RL) that addresses the challenge of online exploration when rewards are not known in advance. Their method leverages Behavioral Foundation Models (BFMs), which are trained on reward-free trajectories to generate optimal policies for any reward function without further learning during transfer. Unlike existing frameworks that require offline knowledge of rewards, this approach treats the problem as a bandit-like exploration-exploitation task, where the BFM recommends policies, interacts with the environment, and receives reward feedback to iteratively converge on the optimal policy. The team developed a formulation inspired by the Upper Confidence Bound algorithm, demonstrating that exploration can be guided by minimizing the eigenvalues of an uncertainty matrix in the context of linear reward approximation. They validated their framework both qualitatively and quantitatively in a simple environment, showing that BFMs can effectively generate exploration policies and enable online learning through trial-and-error interactions, aligning zero-shot transfer more closely with traditional reinforcement learning settings.

item.title: Researchers develop corruption-robust offline reinforcement learning methods with human feedback, providing provable guarantees against adversarial and noisy data corruptions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed new methods for offline reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) that are robust against data corruption, including adversarial attacks and noisy human preferences. Their approach provides provable guarantees for identifying near-optimal policies even when a fraction of the feedback data is corrupted. This work addresses a gap in existing research by combining corruption robustness with offline RLHF, which had previously been studied separately. The proposed methods involve learning a reward model with confidence sets and then deriving a pessimistic optimal policy based on these sets. The researchers leverage offline corruption-robust RL oracles in different ways depending on assumptions about data coverage, enabling effective policy learning despite corrupted data. This represents the first known approach offering theoretical guarantees for corruption-robust offline RLHF.

item.title: Researchers introduce RIFair framework to evaluate Robust Individual Fairness by exposing vulnerabilities in neural networks under semantic-preserving adversarial perturbations across multiple models and datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed RIFair, a new framework designed to evaluate Robust Individual Fairness (RIF) in deep neural networks by identifying vulnerabilities that affect both prediction robustness and fairness under semantic-preserving adversarial perturbations. Unlike existing methods that assess robustness and fairness separately, RIFair exposes critical failure modes where models may behave unfairly or unreliably despite appearing robust or fair when evaluated in isolation. The framework uses a black-box adversarial approach to generate semantically equivalent but challenging instance pairs, revealing hidden biases and robustness issues across various models and real-world textual datasets. The study demonstrates that traditional metrics often overlook complex behaviors such as Robust Biased and Unrobust Fair outcomes, underscoring the importance of considering RIF as a comprehensive criterion for trustworthy model assessment. The researchers have made their experimental code publicly available to support further investigation and development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose a perplexity-based filtering method to mitigate model collapse in large language models without requiring human-authored data, improving diversity and commonsense accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called model collapse in large language models, where training on AI-generated content leads to reduced diversity and a decline in commonsense reasoning. They found that this collapse is linked to an increasing concentration of probability on a small set of tokens and is driven by training on less surprising data. To address this, they propose a perplexity-based filtering method that prioritizes high-surprise documents during fine-tuning, which effectively mitigates model collapse without needing to distinguish between human and AI-generated content. Through extensive simulations across various datasets and language models, the proposed strategy consistently improved performance, sometimes surpassing human-data baselines, while maintaining diversity in generated outputs. This approach offers a scalable and practical solution for training generative AI systems in environments increasingly populated by synthetic data, providing a unified understanding of model collapse and its mitigation.

item.title: Researchers propose a concept-based framework for neuron-level interpretability in deep reinforcement learning, aligning neuron activations with logical formulas to explain decision-making patterns [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new framework to improve interpretability in deep reinforcement learning (DRL) by linking neuron activations to logical formulas composed of semantic concepts. This approach addresses the challenge of explaining DRL models, which often operate in continuous state spaces without predefined semantic concepts, by automatically aligning neuron behaviors with interpretable atomic concepts derived through a value-sensitive discretization of raw state features. The framework provides fine-grained, neuron-level explanations that reveal meaningful decision-making patterns in both continuous and discrete environments, enhancing transparency and trust in DRL systems. The proposed method bridges the gap between continuous signals and symbolic reasoning, enabling explicit explanations of the internal representations within DRL networks. Experimental results demonstrate that this concept-based approach effectively captures strategic decision boundaries relevant to the agent's value assessment, offering explanations that align with human intuition without relying on manual feature engineering.

item.title: Researchers introduce Mantis, a lightweight transformer-based foundation model pre-trained on synthetic data for time series classification, achieving state-of-the-art results across diverse datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Mantis, a lightweight transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for time series classification. Unlike previous models focused mainly on forecasting, Mantis is pre-trained solely on synthetic data using self-supervised contrastive learning. The model introduces a novel token generator unit to improve tokenization, which is crucial for maximizing transformer performance, and employs an advanced test-time method that combines intermediate-layer representations, self-ensembling, and cross-model embedding fusion to enhance accuracy. Extensive testing across four diverse datasets from various application domains shows that Mantis outperforms existing foundation models, setting a new state-of-the-art in time series classification. This advancement highlights the potential of transformer architectures in this under-explored area and suggests new directions for future research and applications in time series analysis.

item.title: Researchers propose a two-stage hallucination detection algorithm using cross-model consistency and uncertainty intervals to improve large language model reliability while reducing computational cost [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a two-stage algorithm to detect hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) by combining self-consistency checks with cross-model consistency verification. This approach uses an additional verifier model selectively, based on uncertainty intervals, to improve detection accuracy while reducing computational costs. The method outperforms existing self-consistency-based techniques and offers a theoretical framework through kernel mean embeddings. Extensive experiments on question-answering benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed algorithm maintains high detection performance and efficiency. This work addresses the limitations of current black-box hallucination detection methods and provides a practical solution for enhancing the reliability of LLMs in sensitive applications.

item.title: Researchers propose SAGE, a search-augmented framework to evaluate large language models on free-form question answering without fixed ground-truth answers, showing strong agreement with human evaluations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced SAGE, a search-augmented evaluation framework designed to assess large language models (LLMs) on free-form question answering tasks without relying on fixed ground-truth answers. SAGE operates by actively retrieving and synthesizing external evidence through iterative web queries, summarization, and reflection, addressing limitations of traditional evaluation methods that depend on static references or ungrounded LLM judgments. Experimental results demonstrate that SAGE achieves substantial to perfect agreement with human evaluations across multiple benchmarks. This approach reduces dependence on costly and incomplete pre-annotated references and mitigates issues where LLMs as evaluators tend to accept incorrect answers or fabricate rationales. By dynamically gathering and refining information from external sources, SAGE offers a scalable and adaptive alternative for evaluating the factual accuracy of LLM outputs in open-ended question answering scenarios.

item.title: Researchers propose TraCeS method to learn per-timestep constraint violation credit from sparse trajectory-level labels for safer reinforcement learning without known cost functions or thresholds [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced TraCeS (Trajectory-based Constraint Estimation for Safety), a new method designed to improve safety in reinforcement learning (RL) when explicit safety constraints are not directly measurable. TraCeS learns to assign per-timestep violation credit from sparse, trajectory-level labels that indicate whether an entire rollout meets an unknown safety threshold. This approach does not require a known cost function or threshold and integrates with standard continuous-control algorithms to enhance constrained policy optimization. The method trains a sequential violation estimator that predicts the probability a trajectory has not violated safety constraints at each step, enabling more precise feedback from coarse supervision signals. The researchers provide theoretical analysis of the learning objective's approximation gap and demonstrate through experiments that TraCeS improves constraint satisfaction and feedback efficiency compared to baseline methods across various continuous-control benchmarks, including long-horizon tasks and scenarios with noisy or inconsistent labels.

item.title: Researchers present physics-constrained fine-tuning framework for flow-matching generative models to enforce PDE constraints and solve inverse problems in scientific systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a framework to fine-tune flow-matching generative models by incorporating physical constraints through partial differential equations (PDEs). This approach starts with models trained on low-fidelity or observational data and applies a differentiable post-training process to ensure physical consistency and boundary condition adherence without altering the learned data distribution. The method also includes a learnable latent parameter predictor to infer unknown physical inputs, enabling the model to solve inverse problems by producing physically valid solutions alongside estimates of hidden parameters. The framework was validated on standard PDE benchmarks, showing improved compliance with PDE constraints and accurate recovery of latent coefficients. By combining generative modeling with scientific inference, this approach offers a data-efficient and physics-aware tool for simulation-augmented discovery and modeling of complex physical systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce Quantum Flow Matching, a quantum-circuit method for efficient interpolation between density matrices enabling generative modeling and observable estimation on quantum computers
item.description: Researchers have developed Quantum Flow Matching (QFM), a quantum-circuit method that efficiently interpolates between two density matrices, extending classical flow matching techniques to quantum systems. QFM enables systematic preparation of quantum states and sample generation for accurate observable estimation, and can be implemented on quantum computers without requiring costly circuit redesigns. This approach offers a unified framework for generative modeling in quantum computing. The team demonstrated QFM's versatility through applications such as generating quantum states with specific magnetization and entanglement entropy, estimating nonequilibrium free-energy differences to test the quantum Jarzynski equality, and accelerating studies of superdiffusion. These results highlight QFM's potential to advance quantum generative modeling and facilitate various quantum physics investigations.

item.title: Researchers systematically compare one-shot and iterative pruning for neural network compression, finding one-shot better at low pruning ratios and iterative better at high ratios, and propose a hybrid approach [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted a systematic comparison of one-shot and iterative pruning methods for neural network compression, revealing that one-shot pruning is more effective at lower pruning ratios, while iterative pruning performs better at higher ratios. They provided rigorous definitions and benchmarks across various pruning settings and criteria, challenging the common preference for iterative pruning. The study introduces a hybrid pruning approach based on patience-based pruning, which can outperform traditional methods in certain cases. This work offers valuable guidance for practitioners in selecting pruning strategies that best fit their specific goals and constraints, with source code made available for further exploration.
