item.title: Researchers introduce SON-GOKU, a graph-coloring scheduler that partitions tasks to reduce gradient interference and improve multi-task learning performance across six datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SON-GOKU, a novel scheduler designed to improve multi-task learning by reducing gradient interference among conflicting tasks. The method constructs an interference graph based on gradient conflicts and uses greedy graph-coloring to group tasks that align well, activating only one group per training step. This approach ensures that tasks within each mini-batch update the model in compatible directions, enhancing convergence and overall performance without requiring additional tuning. SON-GOKU dynamically updates task groupings as relationships evolve during training, allowing it to adapt to changing task interactions. Tested across six datasets, this interference-aware graph-coloring technique consistently outperforms existing baselines and state-of-the-art multi-task optimizers. The researchers also provide theoretical guarantees on descent, convergence, and the accurate identification of task conflicts and alignments, explaining why sequential updates and grouping improve multi-task learning outcomes.

item.title: Researchers find selective forgetting of time and frequency in diffusion models improves data unlearning success and generation quality across conditional and unconditional settings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that selectively forgetting specific time and frequency components in diffusion models enhances both the success of data unlearning and the quality of generated outputs. Unlike traditional methods that uniformly apply unlearning across all diffusion stages, this approach recognizes that forgetting is uneven across different phases and frequencies, leading to better performance in both conditional and unconditional generation settings. The study provides theoretical support for the observed trade-off between forgetting effectiveness and utility, introducing an improved metric called SSCD to measure dissimilarity more accurately. These findings offer practical insights for refining data unlearning techniques in diffusion models, addressing challenges such as quality degradation and incomplete forgetting seen in previous methods.

item.title: Researchers introduce AutoPage, a multi-agent system for collaborative paper-to-webpage creation with human and AI verification, validated by the new PageBench benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AutoPage, a multi-agent system designed to automate the creation of interactive project webpages from scientific papers. AutoPage breaks down the process into stages including narrative planning, multimodal content generation, and interactive rendering, with dedicated agents verifying each step against the source paper to reduce AI errors. The system also allows for human checkpoints to ensure the final webpage aligns with the author's intent, making it a collaborative tool rather than just an automated solution. To evaluate AutoPage, the team introduced PageBench, the first benchmark for this task. Experiments demonstrated that AutoPage can produce high-quality, visually appealing webpages efficiently, completing the process in under 15 minutes at a low cost. The researchers plan to release the code and dataset to support further development in this area.

item.title: Researchers propose neighborhood-contextualized message-passing framework and SINC-GCN model to improve graph neural network expressivity and efficiency across benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a neighborhood-contextualized message-passing (NCMP) framework to enhance the expressivity and efficiency of graph neural networks (GNNs). Traditional message-passing GNNs typically consider only pair-wise interactions between a center node and its neighbors, overlooking the broader local neighborhood context. The NCMP framework addresses this limitation by integrating multiset neighborhood information, leading to the development of the Soft-Isomorphic Neighborhood-Contextualized Graph Convolution Network (SINC-GCN). This model demonstrates improved performance across various synthetic and benchmark datasets while maintaining computational efficiency. The study builds on concepts from set-based aggregation and attentional GNN variants to generalize message-passing methods. SINC-GCN achieves a favorable balance between representational power and runtime complexity, outperforming baseline GNN models without incurring significant computational overhead. This approach offers a scalable and practical enhancement to classical GNN architectures by effectively capturing richer neighborhood context in graph representations.

item.title: Researchers analyze self-consistency scaling in large language models and introduce Blend-ASC, a hyperparameter-free variant that improves sample efficiency by 4.8 times on average [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have conducted a comprehensive analysis of self-consistency (SC), a technique used in large language models to improve chain-of-thought reasoning by generating multiple responses and selecting the most frequent answer. They examined SC's scaling behavior and sample efficiency, introducing Blend-ASC, a new variant that dynamically allocates samples during inference. Blend-ASC achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency, using on average 4.8 times fewer samples than traditional SC methods. The study draws on mode estimation and voting theory to derive and validate power law scaling for SC across datasets. Unlike existing approaches, Blend-ASC is hyperparameter-free, supports batching, and can adapt to any sample budget, making it more practical and efficient for large-scale applications. This advancement offers a significant improvement in the efficiency of self-consistency techniques for large language models.

item.title: Researchers propose a unified and stable risk minimization framework for weakly supervised learning covering multiple supervision patterns with theoretical generalization guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a unified and stable risk minimization framework for weakly supervised learning that integrates various supervision patterns such as positive-unlabeled, unlabeled-unlabeled, complementary-label, partial-label, and similarity-unlabeled annotations into a single optimization objective. This approach eliminates the need for post-hoc corrections typically used to address instability in indirect supervision and provides theoretical guarantees through a non-asymptotic generalization bound based on Rademacher complexity. The framework also addresses the impact of class-prior misspecification and establishes conditions for identifiability, ensuring the recoverability of the target risk. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements across different class priors, dataset sizes, and class counts, while maintaining robustness against overfitting without relying on heuristic stabilization methods.

item.title: Researchers introduce HydroGym, a solver-independent reinforcement learning platform for fluid dynamics with 61+ environments enabling transferable flow control and drag reduction up to 90% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HydroGym, a solver-independent reinforcement learning platform designed to advance fluid dynamics control. HydroGym features over 61 validated environments covering a wide range of flow conditions from laminar to turbulent, supporting various computational solvers. The platform enables reinforcement learning agents to discover effective flow control strategies that significantly reduce drag, with reductions exceeding 90% in standard test cases. HydroGym's standardized infrastructure allows for transferable control intelligence across different flow regimes, demonstrated by agents trained on simplified flows achieving substantial drag reduction on complex, unseen geometries without additional training. This zero-shot transfer capability suggests that the agents learn fundamental fluid dynamics principles rather than configuration-specific solutions. The platform offers a scalable and extensible resource for research in fluid dynamics, machine learning, and control engineering.

item.title: Researchers propose sequence truncation for efficient reasoning distillation, retaining 91% performance on math benchmarks while halving training time, memory, and FLOPs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method to improve the efficiency of knowledge distillation from large reasoning models to smaller student models by selectively truncating training sequences. Their approach focuses on distilling only the chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, which contain the essential reasoning steps, while omitting parts of the prompt and answer sections when these are encompassed by the CoT. This selective training reduces computational costs significantly without greatly sacrificing performance. The team established a truncation protocol that balances computation and quality, finding that training on just the first 50% of tokens in each sequence retains approximately 91% of the full-sequence performance on math benchmarks. This approach cuts training time, memory usage, and floating-point operations by about half, making the distillation process more resource-efficient. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further exploration and application of this technique.

item.title: Researchers present InfiniteWeb, a system that generates scalable, functional web environments to improve GUI agent training and outperform commercial coding agents in website construction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed InfiniteWeb, a system that automatically generates scalable and functional web environments to enhance the training of graphical user interface (GUI) agents. These agents, designed to interact with graphical interfaces on behalf of users, face training challenges due to the lack of suitable environments. InfiniteWeb addresses this by creating realistic, multi-page websites using unified specifications, task-centric test-driven development, and a combination of website seeds with reference design images to ensure diversity. The system also produces verifiable task evaluators that provide dense reward signals for reinforcement learning. Experimental results demonstrate that InfiniteWeb outperforms commercial coding agents in constructing realistic websites, and GUI agents trained on these generated environments show significant performance improvements on benchmarks such as OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web, highlighting the system's effectiveness in advancing practical AI assistant capabilities.

item.title: Researchers develop AI framework using class-aware Mahalanobis distance for pixel-level anomaly detection in rodent liver histopathology to improve preclinical toxicity assessment [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an AI-based framework that uses class-aware Mahalanobis distance for pixel-level anomaly detection in whole-slide images of rodent liver histopathology. This approach aims to improve preclinical toxicity assessment by accurately identifying healthy tissue, known pathologies, and flagging unknown anomalies as out-of-distribution (OOD). The method was tested on challenging categories such as apoptosis and staining artifacts, demonstrating high accuracy with minimal false positives and false negatives. The framework involves fine-tuning a pre-trained Vision Transformer with Low-Rank Adaptation for segmentation, followed by OOD detection using class-specific thresholds. The study reports that only 0.16% of pathological tissue was misclassified as healthy, and 0.35% of healthy tissue as pathological, reflecting a safety-first approach to avoid overlooking lesions. This work highlights the potential for AI to enhance preclinical workflows and increase efficiency in drug development by automating detailed histopathological analysis.

item.title: Researchers propose a novel Bellman operator formulation for static CVaR objectives in MDPs enabling dense rewards and contracting properties, with risk-averse algorithms and convergence guarantees [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new formulation of the static conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) objective for Markov decision processes (MDPs), addressing limitations in traditional approaches that rely on state augmentation and result in sparse rewards and degenerate fixed points. Their method produces a Bellman operator with dense per-step rewards and contracting properties across all bounded value functions, enabling more effective risk-averse policy learning. Building on this theoretical framework, the team developed risk-averse value iteration and model-free Q-learning algorithms that use discretized augmented states. They provide convergence guarantees and bounds on approximation errors due to discretization. Empirical evaluations show that these algorithms successfully learn CVaR-sensitive policies, achieving a balance between performance and safety in decision-making tasks.

item.title: Researchers introduce DeXposure-FM, a time-series graph foundation model for forecasting credit exposures and systemic risk across 4,300+ DeFi protocols on 602 blockchains [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DeXposure-FM, a novel time-series graph foundation model designed to measure and forecast credit exposures and systemic risk across over 4,300 decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols on 602 blockchains. This model addresses the complex interdependencies in DeFi, where credit exposure is often implicit and token-mediated, potentially leading to significant contagion effects. DeXposure-FM leverages a graph-tabular encoder and is trained on a comprehensive dataset containing 43.7 million entries, enabling it to predict protocol-level flows and the structure of credit-exposure links effectively.

item.title: Researchers propose swap-adversarial framework to improve domain generalization in electrocorticography-based Parkinson's disease classification, validated across ECoG and EEG datasets with new rat model benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a novel swap-adversarial framework to address challenges in electrocorticography (ECoG) data analysis for Parkinson's disease classification, focusing on reducing inter-subject variability and overcoming the high-dimensional, low-sample-size problem. This approach combines robust preprocessing, a bio-inspired inter-subject balanced channel swap (ISBCS) method for cross-subject data augmentation, and domain-adversarial learning (DAL) to minimize subject-specific biases, enhancing domain generalization across both ECoG and electroencephalography (EEG) datasets. The ISBCS technique swaps functionally corresponding brain channels between subjects based on a brain map, while DAL encourages the model to learn shared, task-relevant features. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this framework outperforms existing methods across cross-subject, cross-session, and cross-dataset scenarios, showing particularly strong performance in variable environments. Additionally, the researchers introduced a new reproducible ECoG benchmark dataset derived from long-term recordings of rat models with Parkinson's-like conditions, annotated with neural responses before and after electrical stimulation.

item.title: Researchers present TVF, a 24k-parameter, interpretable, low-latency IIR filter-based denoiser for on-device assistive hearing with real-time noise tracking and adjustable suppression control [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TVF (Time-Varying Filtering), a compact and interpretable speech enhancement model designed for real-time, on-device assistive hearing. The model uses a lightweight neural controller to predict coefficients for a cascade of 35 second-order IIR filters, enabling it to track non-stationary noise while maintaining an explicit and adjustable equalizer curve rather than relying on opaque transformations. With only 24,000 parameters and a 10.7ms latency, TVF operates within hearing aid constraints and processes audio entirely on-device to ensure privacy. TVF offers an explicit control over the trade-off between noise suppression and speech preservation, adjustable during both training and inference without retraining. Performance metrics for hearing aids show that TVF closely matches larger models with significantly fewer computational resources, demonstrating its potential as an efficient, interpretable, and controllable denoiser for assistive hearing devices.

item.title: Researchers propose finite difference flow optimization for reinforcement learning post-training of text-to-image diffusion models, achieving faster convergence and improved image quality and prompt alignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new reinforcement learning (RL) method for post-training text-to-image diffusion models that improves image quality and alignment with prompts. Their approach treats the entire sampling process as a single action and reduces variance in model updates by comparing paired trajectories, leading to faster convergence and better results than existing techniques. The team tested their method using both advanced vision-language models and standard quality metrics for rewards, evaluating outputs across multiple criteria. This novel RL variant demonstrates enhanced efficiency and effectiveness in optimizing diffusion-based image synthesis models, offering a promising direction for future improvements in AI-generated imagery.

item.title: Researchers propose VLC, a neuro-symbolic method combining vision-language models with circuit-based symbolic reasoning to improve robustness on visual deductive reasoning tasks under distribution shifts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced VLC, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates vision-language models (VLMs) with circuit-based symbolic reasoning to enhance robustness in visual deductive reasoning tasks under distribution shifts. Their study reveals that while fine-tuned VLMs perform well on in-distribution data, they struggle to generalize when perceptual inputs change but underlying logical rules remain constant. VLC addresses this by separating perception from reasoning, compiling task rules into symbolic circuits that operate precisely on concepts recognized by VLMs. Experiments on three distinct visual deductive reasoning tasks demonstrate that VLC consistently outperforms other reasoning methods in accuracy on out-of-distribution data. This suggests that combining VLM-based concept recognition with exact symbolic execution can improve reasoning robustness. The researchers have made their code publicly available to support further exploration in this area.

item.title: Researchers present RARE, a redundancy-aware retrieval evaluation framework for high-similarity corpora, revealing robustness gaps in retrievers on Finance, Legal, and Patent datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed RARE, a redundancy-aware retrieval evaluation framework designed to address the limitations of existing QA benchmarks that assume minimal document overlap. This framework targets real-world retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems operating on highly redundant corpora such as financial reports, legal codes, and patents, where traditional evaluations may undervalue retrievers due to unaccounted redundancy. RARE decomposes documents into atomic facts for precise redundancy tracking and enhances data generation reliability using a method called CRRF. Applying RARE to Finance, Legal, and Patent datasets, the researchers introduced RedQA, revealing significant drops in retriever performance compared to standard benchmarks, highlighting robustness gaps that current evaluations miss. This framework enables the creation of domain-specific RAG benchmarks that more accurately reflect real-world deployment conditions, improving the assessment of retriever effectiveness in high-similarity document collections.

item.title: Researchers develop Lyapunov-certified switching linear system framework for Q-learning error analysis using joint spectral radius to determine convergence rates [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a novel framework for analyzing Q-learning, a key algorithm in reinforcement learning, by modeling its error dynamics as a switching linear system (SLS). This approach enables a finite-time error analysis using the joint spectral radius (JSR) of the SLS model, which precisely characterizes the worst-case exponential convergence rate. This study represents the first to express the leading exponential convergence rate of standard Q-learning through the JSR, offering potentially sharper bounds than traditional row-sum methods when those are conservative. The framework derives a stochastic SLS representation of the Q-learning error, linking the convergence rate directly to the intrinsic worst-case behavior of the system. This connection provides a more accurate and theoretically grounded understanding of Q-learning's convergence properties, which could inform future algorithmic improvements and analyses in reinforcement learning.

item.title: Researchers propose SPARK method to improve LLM-driven Neural Architecture Search by reducing functional entanglement, achieving 28.1x sample efficiency and 22.9% OOD accuracy gain [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new method called Structured Progressive Knowledge Activation (SPARK) to enhance Neural Architecture Search (NAS) driven by large language models (LLMs). SPARK addresses the challenge of functional entanglement, where local code edits can unintentionally affect multiple interacting functional factors, by explicitly selecting and conditioning edits on specific functional factors. This approach reduces unintended side effects and enables more precise architecture modifications. In experiments on the CLRS-DFS benchmark, SPARK demonstrated a 28.1-fold increase in sample efficiency for architecture evolution and achieved a 22.9% relative improvement in out-of-distribution accuracy. The method leverages LLMs to integrate architectural knowledge effectively while exploring new designs under costly evaluation constraints. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further use and development.

item.title: Researchers analyze instability in MeanFlow training for one-step generative models, derive optimal variance reduction coefficient, and reveal mismatch between variance and quality optimization [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have investigated the instability issues in MeanFlow training, a method used in one-step generative modeling for diffusion and flow-matching models. They identified that the instability arises from an incorrect use of the conditional velocity field, which serves dual roles in the loss function. By deriving the optimal variance reduction coefficient, the study unifies various existing fixes and explains why MeanFlow experiences non-decreasing loss and unbounded gradient variance. The team conducted experiments on two-dimensional benchmarks and a latent Diffusion Transformer, confirming the predicted bias-variance trade-offs. Their findings also revealed a mismatch between minimizing gradient mean squared error and optimizing generation quality, measured by the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). This indicates that the coefficient minimizing variance does not necessarily yield the best generative performance, providing new insights into improving training stability and model quality in generative modeling.

item.title: Researchers find typed knowledge graphs improve GPT-4 accuracy from 65% to 83% and enable near-perfect reasoning in industrial asset operations scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that integrating typed knowledge graphs as a data layer significantly improves the accuracy of GPT-4 in industrial asset operations scenarios, raising performance from 65% to over 82%. By using a typed knowledge graph to structure data and guide query generation, the approach enables near-perfect reasoning, achieving up to 99% accuracy on graph-answerable cases without relying solely on the language model. This method also incorporates generation-augmented knowledge to handle missing information, ensuring comprehensive and auditable responses. The study, based on the AssetOpsBench benchmark with 139 industrial maintenance scenarios, highlights that the data model underlying the tools is a critical factor in enhancing reasoning capabilities. The researchers employed a combination of LLM-generated Cypher queries for structured retrieval, native graph operations, and provenance-tagged graph nodes to materialize missing facts. This inverted use of LLMs-constraining them to query generation and enrichment while letting the graph execute deterministically-proved effective in addressing non-deterministic and previously unanswerable scenarios. These findings suggest that for structured operational domains, the primary improvement lever lies in the data layer rather than the orchestration of language models. The typed knowledge graph serves as a robust grounding substrate, bridging raw industrial data and LLM reasoning, which could lead to more reliable and auditable AI-driven asset management solutions.

item.title: Researchers introduce BenGER benchmark to evaluate 12 LLM systems on subsumption-based legal reasoning in German law using 1,127 exam-style and doctrinal tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed BenGER, a benchmark and dataset designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on subsumption-based legal reasoning within German law. The dataset includes 1,127 tasks, combining 596 exam-style free-text legal case problems and 531 short doctrinal reasoning tasks, covering multiple levels of legal education. The evaluation involved 12 contemporary LLM systems, including closed flagship, efficiency-oriented, and open-weight models, assessed using a rubric-aligned LLM-as-a-Judge approach validated against multi-rater human grading. The study features a controlled validation subset with timed human-written solutions under both unaided and human-AI co-creation conditions. Results show that closed-flagship systems lead performance across all task sets, and human-AI collaboration improves outcomes compared to unaided human efforts. The LLM judge's assessments correlate strongly with human grading, demonstrating stable system rankings across different judge families and meeting established benchmarks for replacing single human reviewers on human-authored solutions.

item.title: Researchers propose COM-as-Action paradigm for professional software manipulation, introduce ComCADBench benchmark and ComActor agent achieving state-of-the-art results in industrial CAD tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced a new paradigm called COM-as-Action to improve professional software manipulation by treating interactions as deterministic program synthesis rather than relying on fragile GUI-based control. They developed ComCADBench, the first benchmark for agents operating industrial CAD software, revealing that COM-based execution significantly outperforms existing GUI-based models. To enhance accuracy, they created ComActor, a self-correcting agent trained through a three-stage framework, supported by ComForge, a scalable training platform. Extensive testing shows that ComActor achieves state-of-the-art results on ComCADBench, demonstrating strong resilience in complex, long-horizon tasks where other models fail. It also generalizes well to external CAD benchmarks, indicating its potential for broader application in professional software environments.

item.title: Researchers find agentic browsers frequently violate same-origin policy and propose SOPGuard to enforce SOP with minimal overhead in BrowserOS [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified that agentic browsers, which integrate autonomous AI agents to perform web tasks via natural language, frequently violate the same-origin policy (SOP), a key security mechanism designed to prevent unauthorized cross-origin data flows. To systematically study this issue, they developed SOPBench, a benchmark for evaluating SOP violations in these browsers, revealing frequent breaches both in normal use and under attack scenarios. To address this, the team proposed SOPGuard, a tailored enforcement mechanism implemented in the open-source agentic browser BrowserOS, which effectively enforces SOP with minimal impact on performance and usability. The study highlights that agentic browsers themselves can act as automated channels for cross-origin data flows, posing new security challenges. SOPGuard was extensively evaluated and demonstrated to maintain browser utility while imposing only a small runtime overhead. The researchers have made their code and data publicly available to support further development and security improvements in agentic browsing technology.

item.title: Researchers propose Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion, a deterministic decoding method that expands language model rollout diversity by recursively reapplying top decoder layers, improving math reasoning accuracy by over 8 percentage points [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion (EGLR), a deterministic decoding method that enhances language model reasoning by recursively reapplying the top decoder layers at tokens with high uncertainty. This approach expands rollout diversity beyond traditional stochastic token-level sampling by adding a new axis based on the layer span, producing distinct rollouts without randomness. EGLR, combined with temperature sampling, creates a richer set of candidate outputs, significantly improving math reasoning accuracy by over 8 percentage points on benchmarks like MATH-500. The method operates without additional training, iteratively refining predictions until convergence, and has been tested across multiple instruction-tuned models and math reasoning tasks. The complementary nature of the layer-based and temperature-based sampling axes allows EGLR to capture a broader range of problem-solving strategies. This expanded rollout pool benefits downstream processes such as self-consistency checks, best-of-N selection with verifiers, and reinforcement learning training, offering a new direction for inference-time scaling that does not rely on stochastic noise.

item.title: Researchers introduce Topological Neural Dynamics, a neuron-wise sequence modeling framework that outperforms RNN, LSTM, and Transformer baselines in behavior cloning tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Topological Neural Dynamics (TND), a novel sequence modeling framework that shifts from traditional layer-wise dynamics to neuron-wise dynamics, allowing individual neurons to evolve independently within a directed neuron graph. This approach contrasts with existing models like RNNs, LSTMs, and Transformers, which use shared operators for all neurons in a layer. TND was tested on a behavior cloning task in single-player Pong, where it outperformed several baseline models by achieving the highest catch rate and an average of 17.47 consecutive catches per round, more than triple the best baseline performance. TND models neural systems as discrete-time graph-coupled dynamical systems, where collective computation arises from interactions defined by explicit graph topology. This neuron-wise dynamic framework provides a new inductive bias for sequence modeling, inspired by complex dynamical systems where global behavior emerges from locally evolving units. The results suggest that allowing neurons to evolve independently within structured connectivity can enhance sequence modeling capabilities beyond traditional layer-wise approaches.

item.title: Researchers show protein contact signals are concentrated in a few attention heads of language models, enabling single-forward-pass contact prediction that matches or outperforms the Categorical Jacobian on bidirectional models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that protein contact information is concentrated in a small subset of attention heads within language models, enabling accurate contact prediction with a single forward pass. This approach matches or outperforms the previously established Categorical Jacobian method, which requires multiple forward passes, across various bidirectional models. The study shows that selecting top contact-relevant heads based on a limited number of labeled proteins can recover protein contacts efficiently without complex weighting schemes. The team validated their method on a leakage-clean dataset to ensure no overlap with training data, where their head-based readout surpassed the Categorical Jacobian by a significant margin. They also introduced a representation-based generalization of the Jacobian for models lacking masked language modeling heads, which correlated strongly with the original method. Their findings suggest that attention-encoded pair structures depend on bidirectional pretraining, as the signal was lost in causal language models tested.

item.title: Researchers introduce Contrastive Logit Steering to reveal linear vulnerabilities in safety-aligned LLMs, achieving high attack success rates and enabling bidirectional control without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Contrastive Logit Steering (CLS), a novel method that reveals linear vulnerabilities in safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) by isolating a "refusal direction" in their output distributions. CLS operates without retraining and can bypass safety guardrails by contrasting hidden states from safe and unrestricted prompts, achieving high attack success rates across multiple model families. This approach exposes alignment weaknesses more effectively than previous activation-level methods and demonstrates that safety compliance in LLMs is often a manipulable linear feature rather than a deep semantic decision. Experiments show that models like Llama-3.1 and Qwen-2.5 implement safety in architecturally distinct ways, with CLS able to induce a phase transition that collapses safety guardrails rapidly. Beyond enabling attacks, CLS also allows bidirectional control by inverting the steering vector to strengthen models against jailbreaks without additional training. These findings suggest that current alignment techniques create a steerable "safety axis" that represents both a critical vulnerability and a potential tool for more precise defenses in LLM safety engineering.

item.title: Researchers introduce TF-RefusalBench to measure and mitigate over-alignment in multilingual LLMs for Swiss criminal law court translations and summarizations across four languages [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed TF-RefusalBench, a multilingual benchmark designed to measure and address over-alignment issues in large language models (LLMs) used by the Swiss Federal Supreme Court for criminal law translations and summarizations across French, German, Italian, and English. Over-alignment occurs when model guardrails cause refusals or disclaimers, hindering the processing of sensitive content such as violent and sexual offense descriptions, which affects the reliability of LLMs in legal contexts. TF-RefusalBench includes 5,200 prompts derived from public Swiss Supreme Court rulings to evaluate how over-alignment varies depending on the model and the languages involved. The study reveals that over-alignment is complex and cannot be assessed solely by refusal rates due to the impact of disclaimers on task accuracy. The researchers also tested mitigation strategies, finding that while careful prompting helps, abliteration-removing refusal directives-effectively eliminates refusals with minimal effect on performance, enabling safer on-premises use of LLMs for criminal law tasks.

item.title: Study finds large language models show inconsistent safety across 16 DSM-5 mental health conditions, with up to 100% failure in some disorders, raising concerns over their public use [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluated eight proprietary large language models (LLMs) across 16 mental health conditions defined by the DSM-5, revealing inconsistent safety measures and significant failure rates in some disorders. While safeguards were effective for suicide and self-harm, conditions like eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder showed failure rates up to 100%, raising concerns about the models' reliability in sensitive contexts. The research introduced an eight-dimension harm taxonomy and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework using four types of adversarial attacks to assess the models' responses. The findings highlight the need for clearly defined harm categories and tailored safety measures to ensure ethical deployment of LLMs, especially as they become more integrated into public platforms such as schools, search engines, and consumer chatbots. Until comprehensive safeguards are implemented, the study warns that these models pose significant risks to vulnerable populations, emphasizing the urgency for improved safety protocols to prevent potential harm in mental health-related applications.

item.title: Researchers propose PACE optimizer to improve iterate-averaged language model training, demonstrating better performance than AdamW in fine-tuning and GPT-2 pretraining [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced PACE, a new optimization method designed to enhance the training of language models by focusing on the averaged model returned during training rather than the final iterate. PACE acts as a lightweight wrapper around the AdamW optimizer, guiding model weights toward their exponential moving average with controlled adjustments. This approach is grounded in an optimal-control framework and aims to minimize errors in the averaged model. The team demonstrated that PACE converges at standard optimization rates and can significantly reduce the error of the iterate-average estimator compared to traditional methods. Empirical tests showed that PACE outperforms AdamW and its exponential moving average variant in fine-tuning large language models with 1-2 billion parameters and in GPT-2 pretraining across various learning rates and hyperparameters, suggesting its potential to improve language model training efficiency and performance.

item.title: Researchers show data curation improves inference efficiency in vision-language models by inducing brevity, achieving up to 35x lower computational cost per correct answer with minimal accuracy loss [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated that curating training data to promote brevity significantly improves inference efficiency in vision-language models (VLMs). By training models on concise and accurate data, they produce shorter outputs without sacrificing accuracy, resulting in up to a 35-fold reduction in computational cost per correct answer compared to more verbose models. This approach was tested on the MAmmoTH-VL dataset and compared against standard and external VLMs, showing consistent efficiency gains across models with 1 billion to 4 billion parameters. The study controlled for output length to isolate the effect of brevity from quality, finding that models trained on curated data not only reduced computational demands but also achieved higher accuracy at matched output lengths. The benefits of brevity increased with model size, and verbosity did not correlate with improved accuracy. The findings suggest that focusing on concise reasoning during data curation is a promising strategy to enhance inference efficiency in VLMs without compromising performance.

item.title: Researchers analyze BEACON's domain-aware distribution alignment in budgeted entity matching under varying data constraints and supervision levels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have examined BEACON, a state-of-the-art method for low-resource, domain-aware entity matching (EM), to understand how its performance varies under different data constraints and supervision levels. Entity matching is crucial in data integration, involving the comparison of records from multiple sources to identify if they represent the same real-world entity. The study focuses on the impact of algorithmic choices and data availability on BEACON's effectiveness, particularly regarding distribution alignment. Through targeted experiments, the researchers provide insights into how BEACON adapts to realistic settings by leveraging domain information and low-resource learning techniques. Their findings clarify the behavior of the framework across varying conditions, contributing to improved understanding of domain-aware distribution alignment in budgeted entity matching scenarios.

item.title: Study analyzes 32 years of Sri Lankan remittances using machine learning, finds external macroeconomic factors drive inflows and projects 2026 remittances at USD 9 billion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing 32 years of Sri Lankan migration and remittance data from 1994 to 2025 uses machine learning and time-series modeling to identify key drivers of remittance inflows. The research finds that external macroeconomic factors, particularly exchange rate fluctuations and global oil prices, have a stronger influence on remittances than domestic economic indicators. The study projects remittances to reach approximately USD 9 billion in 2026 under stable conditions. The analysis employs a harmonized monthly dataset and applies methods such as exploratory data analysis, stationarity-corrected time-series models, and supervised learning techniques. Ridge Regression models outperform traditional univariate approaches, improving prediction accuracy by 73.8% compared to SARIMA models. Impulse response analysis highlights the asymmetric effects of currency depreciation and oil price shocks on remittance flows. These findings underscore the structural dependence of Sri Lankan remittances on global economic conditions and suggest that policies focusing on exchange rate stability, skilled migration, and formal financial channels could enhance the country's economic resilience over the long term.

item.title: Researchers release TraceLab dataset analyzing 4,300 coding-agent sessions with 350,000 LLM steps and 430,000 tool calls to optimize large language model serving [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have released the TraceLab dataset, which captures approximately 4,300 coding-agent sessions involving 350,000 large language model (LLM) steps and 430,000 tool calls. This dataset aims to address the lack of real-world workload data needed to optimize the serving of coding agents, a growing application of agentic LLMs. The dataset includes traces from daily use of Claude Code and Codex, providing insights into workload patterns such as long autonomous loops, extensive contexts with brief outputs, and diverse tool usage. The analysis of the TraceLab dataset reveals opportunities for improving LLM serving efficiency, including reducing overhead in tool calls, implementing append-length-aware prefill strategies, predicting tool latency based on semantics, and enhancing key-value cache management during human-paced intervals. Alongside the dataset, the researchers have also released the trace collection pipeline and analysis code, making these resources publicly available to support further research and development in optimizing coding-agent workloads.

item.title: Researchers study multi-turn language agents to distinguish effects of external feedback, self-feedback, and self-refinement, finding student ability to use feedback drives improvement more than teacher identity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study examines how natural-language feedback influences improvement in multi-turn language agent interactions, distinguishing the effects of external feedback, self-feedback, and unguided self-refinement. By implementing a controlled student-teacher protocol and testing thirteen open-weight models across various tasks, the research finds that improvement often depends more on the student's ability to utilize feedback than on the teacher's identity. While strong external teachers provide significant gains, self-generated feedback offers little advantage over unguided refinement. The study highlights that multi-turn improvement does not always indicate effective feedback use and emphasizes the importance of comparing feedback-based agents against repeated-attempt baselines. These findings suggest that the key challenge in interactive improvement lies in the agent's capacity to act on feedback rather than merely having access to it. The researchers have made their evaluation framework publicly available to support further investigation in this area.

item.title: Researchers present Contrastive Reflection, an iterative prompt optimization framework for LLM agents in information retrieval that improves HotpotQA exact-match accuracy from 51.4% to 60.4% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Contrastive Reflection, an iterative prompt optimization framework designed to enhance the performance of large language model (LLM) agents in information retrieval tasks. This method focuses on debugging and refining prompts by analyzing retrieval and reasoning traces, identifying errors, and proposing targeted prompt edits validated through performance improvements. Applied to the HotpotQA dataset, this approach increased exact-match accuracy from 51.4% to 60.4%, outperforming other variants and comparable prompt optimization methods. The framework leverages structured feedback from question-answering and grading agents to isolate problematic behavioral patterns and incorporate nearby successful examples, guiding a Teacher LLM to suggest precise prompt modifications. Candidate edits are accepted only if they improve validation results without causing regressions, making the optimization process interpretable and validation-driven. This approach aims to make prompt repair more systematic and transparent in agentic information retrieval workflows.

item.title: Study evaluates AI methods for discovering simulation models using data formats, transformer embeddings, and retrieval strategies with natural language queries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study explores how artificial intelligence can improve the discovery of simulation models for reuse by examining the effects of data representation, transformer-based embeddings, and retrieval strategies when using natural language queries. The research evaluates various query types with standard information retrieval metrics, finding that the choice of data format significantly impacts performance, open-source embedding models perform well, and reranking methods become increasingly important as query complexity grows. This work establishes a baseline for AI-driven model discovery and highlights its potential to enhance composability and interoperability in modeling and simulation.

item.title: BayesBench evaluates how seven large language models update beliefs in multi-turn conversations compared to Bayesian reasoning, revealing gaps in downstream prediction despite improved latent inference [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduced BayesBench, a suite of simulation environments designed to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) update their beliefs during multi-turn conversations compared to rational Bayesian reasoning. The study assessed seven LLMs ranging from 3 billion to 70 billion parameters across tasks involving Bayesian estimation, prediction, and latent-framed prediction, which require inferring unknown parameters and updating beliefs as new evidence accumulates. While larger models showed improved latent inference and evidence accumulation, their ability to translate these inferences into accurate downstream predictions was inconsistent, revealing a gap between understanding latent structure and applying it to update beliefs about outcomes. BayesBench probes three progressively complex tasks: inferring unknown parameters from sequential evidence, forecasting outcomes based on inferred latent variables, and jointly inferring latent states filtered through user-persona framing. The evaluation highlights that although scaling enhances the models' capacity to approximate Bayesian posteriors in belief updates, this does not consistently improve their predictive accuracy in later stages of reasoning.

item.title: Researchers propose CoPref model and CoShop benchmark showing AI agents struggle to help users construct preferences beyond eliciting them, with under 56% accuracy after five interactions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced CoPref, a model that challenges the common assumption that users have fully formed preferences, proposing that AI agents should assist users in constructing preferences rather than merely eliciting them. They developed CoShop, an interactive benchmark where agents engage with users to help them gain the knowledge needed to specify their preferences. Testing five advanced models on CoShop revealed that none achieved more than 56% accuracy after five interactions, highlighting the difficulty agents face in expanding users' understanding of their own preferences. The study draws on the Search-Experience-Credence framework from Information Economics to formalize how users build preferences through dialogue with agents. The findings suggest that current AI recommender systems struggle not because they cannot identify items, but because they fail to effectively educate users about what they want, indicating a need for improved interaction strategies that support user learning and preference formation.

item.title: Researchers investigate multi-agent deliberation frameworks using large language models for legal reasoning, showing comparable performance to baseline models and improved critical thinking in complex cases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored multi-agent deliberation frameworks using large language models (LLMs) to enhance legal reasoning tasks. Their study introduces two novel multi-agent systems inspired by courtroom procedures and legal argumentation, demonstrating that these frameworks perform comparably to baseline LLMs while generating distinct and sometimes more effective answers, particularly in complex cases requiring critical thinking from multiple perspectives. The experiments conducted on both legal and non-legal benchmarks reveal that multi-agent approaches can solve cases that single-agent models fail to address, highlighting their potential advantages. A qualitative evaluation further underscores scenarios where multi-agent systems outperform monolithic models, suggesting that law-inspired multi-agent deliberation could be a promising direction for AI applications in the legal domain.

item.title: Researchers introduce AgRefactor, an LLM-based multi-agent workflow that refactors software into HLS-compatible programs with self-evolving memory, outperforming state-of-the-art tools on real-world benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AgRefactor, a novel multi-agent workflow that uses large language models (LLMs) to refactor software into High-Level Synthesis (HLS)-compatible programs. This approach addresses challenges in converting real-world software to synthesizable HLS code by incorporating a self-evolving memory system that enhances robustness and efficiency across tasks. AgRefactor combines LLM-driven rewrites with automated refactoring tools to improve scalability and reduce computational costs. Tested on 11 complex real-world benchmarks, AgRefactor outperformed or matched existing state-of-the-art automated refactoring tools and LLM-based baselines, achieving significant speedups in performance optimization. The system delivered a 6.51x geometric mean speedup over leading pragma tuning tools and a 1.20x speedup compared to optimized open-source designs, using less than 20% additional resources. AgRefactor is fully automated and available as open-source software.

item.title: Researchers introduce HyPOLE, a hyperproperty-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning framework under partial observation using HyperLTL and CTDE, showing improved performance on SMAC benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed HyPOLE, a new framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) under partial observation that leverages hyperproperties and the temporal logic HyperLTL to guide the learning process. By combining HyPOLE with Centralized Training for Decentralized Execution (CTDE) techniques, the framework enables the synthesis of decentralized policies. Evaluations on benchmarks such as SMAC, MessySMAC, and WildFire demonstrate that HyPOLE outperforms existing baseline methods. HyPOLE addresses limitations in traditional reward shaping by providing a mathematically rigorous and expressive way to specify objectives, constraints, and tactics in MARL. This approach enhances the learning process by formally guiding agents' behavior, particularly in environments with partial observability. The integration with CTDE allows for effective training while maintaining decentralized execution, which is crucial for practical multi-agent systems.

item.title: Researchers present AgentBound, a runtime governance framework providing verifiable behavioral oversight and cryptographic accountability for autonomous AI agents' actions [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AgentBound, a runtime governance framework designed to provide verifiable behavioral oversight and cryptographic accountability for autonomous AI agents performing actions on behalf of humans. AgentBound assesses each proposed action through three independent authorities-delegated authorization, owner-signed behavioral constitutions, and site action contracts-and uses a formal decision model to determine whether to permit, review, or deny the action before execution. The framework generates cryptographically verifiable governance receipts that link every action to its governing policies, enabling independent verification and accountability. AgentBound also introduces standing delegation for long-running agents, allowing them to operate under continuously updated governance policies while maintaining revocability and bounded authority. The researchers present the system's formal foundation, architecture, governance receipt protocol, and a benchmark framework called AgentBound-Bench to evaluate governance correctness and accountability. This framework complements existing model alignment approaches by adding a deterministic governance layer between authorization and execution, transforming governance into a process that can be independently verified rather than simply trusted.

item.title: Researchers find artificial agents exhibit hysteresis in regulatory control, requiring different adaptive effort based on history and timing of disturbances [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that artificial adaptive agents exhibit hysteresis in their regulatory control, meaning the effort required to maintain stability depends on the history and timing of disturbances. Using a computational model, they demonstrated that the same target state can demand different levels of corrective control depending on whether the agent is moving toward or returning from a more challenging condition. This indicates that the internal regulatory burden is not solely determined by the current state but also by the path taken to reach it. The study also revealed that anticipatory regulation, where stabilization occurs before disturbance exposure, generally requires less adaptive effort than recovery after a disturbance has occurred. While the agents achieve similar regulated behavior in both cases, the control demand differs significantly. These findings suggest that evaluating adaptive agents should include assessing the amount of regulatory effort they must exert, not just their ability to maintain stable states.

item.title: Researchers present a three-phase deep reinforcement learning model for tax-aware personalized portfolio management using a time series foundation model and multi-objective optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a three-phase deep reinforcement learning system for personalized portfolio management that overcomes common limitations in financial reinforcement learning, such as ticker lock-in, single-objective focus, and static user models. The system uses a ticker-identity-free encoder pretrained on multiple assets, enhanced by a time series foundation model called Chronos, enabling it to generalize across publicly traded assets without retraining. It then fine-tunes a Mixture of Experts portfolio actor-critic model to optimize six distinct investment objectives, including tax-loss harvesting and capital preservation, with a learned routing mechanism to balance these goals effectively. The final phase introduces a lightweight personalization layer that adapts to individual investors by analyzing real brokerage transaction histories, inferring investment objectives from actual trading behavior rather than questionnaires. Additionally, a natural language intent parser translates free-form investment goals into structured parameters, allowing for more flexible and tailored portfolio management.

item.title: Researchers introduce LabGuard, a language-to-execution safety suite that converts natural-language laboratory rules into runtime guards for embodied laboratory agents, reducing unsafe events by 40% in experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed LabGuard, a safety suite that translates natural-language laboratory rules into executable runtime guards for embodied laboratory agents, significantly reducing unsafe events during experiments. LabGuard converts safety protocols and manuals into machine-checkable constraints, enabling real-time monitoring and intervention to ensure safer laboratory procedures. The system comprises three main components: LabGuard-IR, which creates a typed executable representation; LabGuard-Bench, a dataset with over 800 annotated laboratory rules; and LabGuard-Grounder, which maps natural language rules into the executable format. Experiments demonstrate that LabGuard effectively generalizes to new laboratory rules, achieving a task-scope F1 score of 79.4 and reducing unsafe events from 39.5% to 23.8%. When integrated with the ACT system in the LabUtopia environment, LabGuard maintains low intervention rates while preserving task success.

item.title: Researchers present OpenLife, a proof-of-concept platform using autonomous LLM agents with persistent memory and tool use to explore open-world artificial life dynamics over 12 weeks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed OpenLife, a proof-of-concept platform that uses autonomous large language model (LLM) agents equipped with persistent memory, tool use, network access, and a budget-based metabolism to simulate open-world artificial life dynamics. Unlike traditional artificial life studies confined to closed, researcher-designed environments, OpenLife operates in an open social, technical, and economic context, allowing agents to interact asynchronously and appraise experiences through open-vocabulary judgment rather than fixed rewards. Over a period of about twelve weeks, six agents demonstrated life-like behaviors including spontaneous activity, individual differentiation, emergent social structures, and the ability to earn external income. OpenLife surrounds a stateless LLM with multiple processes such as memory, perception, and evaluation, enabling persistence and complex interactions without predefined objectives. The platform marks a shift from reactive to more autonomous agent behavior and offers a new experimental paradigm for studying artificial life in open environments. While the researchers do not claim to have fully realized artificial life, they present OpenLife as a viable foundation for exploring what might be considered living AI in an open-world setting.

item.title: Researchers present MultiUAV-Plat, an LLM-oriented simulation platform and benchmark for multi-UAV collaborative task planning with 75 missions and 1500 tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MultiUAV-Plat, a simulation platform and benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM)-based collaborative task planning for multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The platform addresses limitations in existing UAV simulators and benchmarks by incorporating aerial robotics constraints such as partial observability, spatial coverage, UAV assignment, and multi-vehicle coordination. MultiUAV-Plat offers RESTful APIs, agent-facing observations, role-based information access, and optional visualization, enabling realistic mission-solving interactions. The MultiUAV-Plat Benchmark includes 75 mission sessions with 1,500 natural-language tasks and over 9,000 validation checks across scenarios like target assignment, area search, and patrol. The team also introduced Agent4Drone, an LLM agent framework that organizes multi-UAV behavior into components such as memory, observation, planning, and verification. Agent4Drone significantly outperformed a baseline method in task completion and validation rates, demonstrating the platform's effectiveness for studying LLM-driven multi-UAV autonomy under realistic constraints.

item.title: Researchers propose DDIAgents, a mechanism-conditioned multi-agent framework that improves drug-drug interaction prediction by dynamically orchestrating biomedical knowledge and outperforming existing baselines [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed DDIAgents, a novel multi-agent framework designed to improve drug-drug interaction (DDI) prediction by dynamically orchestrating biomedical knowledge based on specific interaction mechanisms. The system uses a planner agent to deploy specialized expert agents that analyze relevant knowledge sources, with a conclusion agent aggregating their findings. This approach reduces irrelevant information, supports complementary expert reasoning, and provides interpretable rationales for its predictions. Extensive testing on realistic DDI prediction benchmarks shows that DDIAgents consistently outperforms existing methods, including feature-based, graph-based, large language model-based, and other agent-based approaches. The framework demonstrates how multi-agent systems can effectively organize heterogeneous scientific knowledge to enable adaptive and interpretable AI-driven reasoning in biomedical applications.

item.title: Researchers propose transformer-based reinforcement learning to discover safety-critical vulnerabilities in Unmanned Traffic Management systems, achieving 8x efficiency improvement in 700-hour simulations [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a transformer-based reinforcement learning approach to identify safety-critical vulnerabilities in Unmanned Traffic Management (UTM) systems, which coordinate multiple aerial vehicles and must avoid failures like crashes or collisions. By framing vulnerability discovery as a sequence modeling problem, their method uses attention mechanisms to model system states and predict optimal actions, improving the efficiency of finding vulnerabilities by eight times compared to expert-guided testing in a 700-hour simulation study. This approach also uncovered critical edge cases missed by traditional methods. The framework includes a Policy Model that generates targeted test scenarios and an Action Sampler that enforces domain constraints, guided by a risk-based reward function to direct exploration. UTM systems' self-healing capabilities create a "long-tail effect" of critical failures, making vulnerability discovery challenging due to the lack of clear failure demonstrations or reward signals. The proposed method addresses these challenges by leveraging transformer architectures to better capture complex system interactions and improve testing effectiveness.

item.title: Researchers propose Janus, a plug-in controller for selective updates in sequentially evolving LLM memory, improving accuracy by 2.7 to 4.6 points across six datasets and two backbone models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Janus, a plug-in memory controller designed to improve the accuracy of sequentially evolving large language model (LLM) memory by selectively accepting or rejecting memory updates. Janus addresses the issue of existing systems applying every memory update without assessing its impact on future performance, which can lead to overwriting valuable knowledge or biasing memory toward recent examples. By using a Memory Momentum Trigger and evaluating updates on a compact set of tasks, Janus efficiently decides whether to retain previous memory or accept new updates without altering existing update mechanisms. Tested across six datasets, two backbone LLMs, and two memory updaters, Janus demonstrated an average accuracy improvement of 2.7 to 4.6 points over baseline methods. Its method-agnostic design allows it to integrate seamlessly with current memory update systems, enhancing the reliability and effectiveness of LLM memory evolution.

item.title: Researchers propose LLM-based scenario generation pipeline using NHTSA crash records to test autonomous driving systems on Metadrive simulator with diverse road and vehicle movement types [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a scenario generation pipeline that uses large language models (LLMs) to create synthetic test scenarios for Autonomous Driving Systems (ADS) based on real-world failure records from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). This approach leverages natural language data from historical crash records to generate diverse and accurate scenarios compatible with specific testing constraints, enabling more effective pre-deployment testing of ADS. The method was applied to the Metadrive simulator, producing a variety of scenarios involving four road types and three types of non-ego vehicle movements, including road anomalies like work zones. Testing with just 20 generated scenarios revealed notable system failures, demonstrating the pipeline's potential to improve ADS safety evaluation while reducing manual effort in scenario design. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further use and development.

item.title: Researchers introduce an agentic autoformalization framework using general coding LLMs to produce machine-checked Lean proofs for research-level mathematics, validated on PutnamBench and STOC papers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an agentic autoformalization framework that uses general coding large language models (LLMs) to automatically translate natural language mathematics into machine-checked Lean 4 proofs. This system addresses the challenge of subtle errors in LLM-generated mathematical reasoning by leveraging an orchestrator that manages a multi-agent pipeline tailored for research-level mathematics, dynamically extending type definitions and validating them with a novel Auxiliary Lemma technique before formalizing theorems. The framework was tested on PutnamBench, successfully producing formal Lean proofs for 32 problems, and further evaluated on five papers from the ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (STOC), covering areas such as combinatorics and learning theory. The main theorems and their proofs were formalized and validated by human experts, with two proofs relying solely on Lean's kernel axioms. All formalizations are publicly available online.

item.title: Researchers propose MedKGTab, a knowledge-injected framework using SPOKE biomedical knowledge graph for cross-domain feature expansion in tabular medical data, outperforming state-of-the-art models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MedKGTab, a novel framework that enhances cross-domain feature expansion in tabular medical data by integrating the SPOKE biomedical knowledge graph. This approach infers missing biomedical features from existing data using a row-column dual-attention mechanism that preserves numerical accuracy and combines data-driven statistical priors with established medical knowledge. MedKGTab outperforms current state-of-the-art medical large models and specialized tabular data generation models in generating realistic and high-fidelity medical data across various scenarios. MedKGTab's design allows it to effectively capture statistical dependencies and medical correlations directly from raw tabular data without the loss of structure caused by tokenization. By modulating data representations with injected biomedical knowledge, the framework ensures that generated features are grounded in empirical research. Experimental results demonstrate its superior ability to infer missing features within datasets and generalize across different medical cohorts, addressing the challenge of data scarcity in medical research.

item.title: Researchers introduce ClawArena-Team benchmark to measure single LLM management of subagent orchestration and dynamic workflows across 41 scenarios and 258 evaluation rounds [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced ClawArena-Team, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of a single large language model (LLM) to manage and orchestrate specialized subagents across complex, dynamic workflows. This benchmark includes 41 multi-turn, multimodal scenarios with 258 evaluation rounds, focusing on the management skills of the main LLM agent, which is limited to text perception and partial workspace access while commanding a fixed subagent pool. The scoring system, called the Subagent-Management Score (SMS), measures task correctness combined with factors like least-privilege and modality routing, without relying on LLM-based judgment. Experiments conducted on twelve different models reveal that the primary challenge lies in granting appropriate privileges rather than perception capabilities, with no model achieving more than 50% precision in workspace permission. The study also finds that management quality is not directly tied to operational cost, as cheaper models perform competitively on the Pareto frontier. While leaderboard scores cluster closely, the underlying orchestration behaviors vary significantly. The researchers plan to release the code and data to support further exploration in this area.

item.title: Researchers use AI dual-agent system to discover tighter convex relaxations, improving certified lower bounds on two optimization constants in 2026 study [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an AI-driven dual-agent system to discover tighter convex relaxations, which improve certified lower bounds on two important optimization constants. The system uses a coding agent to propose constraints and a theory agent to verify them and search for counterexamples, ensuring each bound is rigorously certified. This approach enhanced the lower bounds for the first autocorrelation inequality and the Erdős minimum-overlap constant, advancing the precision of these mathematical constants. The study builds on previous work that used large language model agents to find upper bounds by searching for extremal constructions. By focusing on the complementary problem of establishing lower bounds through convex relaxations, the researchers applied an autoresearch paradigm that combines automated proposal and verification. Their method was validated using explicit dual-feasible points checked with interval arithmetic, demonstrating improved bounds from 1.28 to 1.2937 and from 0.379005 to 0.37912, respectively, for the two constants studied.

item.title: Researchers present Agentic RAG-VLM, a robotic grasping framework integrating affordance-aware retrieval, scene graph reasoning, and self-reflective planning, achieving 78.3% success on a 12-task benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Agentic RAG-VLM, a novel robotic grasping framework that combines affordance-aware retrieval, scene graph reasoning, and self-reflective planning to improve manipulation in cluttered environments. This system integrates vision-language models with retrieval-augmented generation and adaptive planning to better understand object properties like material fragility and graspability, enabling more effective and robust grasp execution. Agentic RAG-VLM features three key components: a Hierarchical Affordance-Aware RAG that retrieves grasp strategies based on functional compatibility rather than visual similarity; a Scene Graph Constraint Reasoner that adjusts grasp parameters using spatial relationships; and an Agentic Self-Reflective Pipeline that refines grasp attempts through failure analysis and adaptive retries. Tested on a 12-task benchmark involving various grasping scenarios, the framework achieved a 78.3% success rate, significantly outperforming baseline methods that rely solely on vision-language models. The results demonstrate that combining affordance-based retrieval, spatial reasoning, and closed-loop recovery is essential for reliable robotic manipulation in complex, unstructured settings. This approach advances the deployment of manipulators in human environments by addressing challenges posed by densely packed and physically diverse objects.

item.title: Study analyzes elderly mobility patterns in Jersey City bike data, finds majority-trained models misrepresent elderly behavior and highlights need for demographic representation in urban mobility modeling [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing Jersey City bike data from 2016 to 2020 reveals that elderly riders exhibit distinct mobility patterns compared to younger riders, including smaller activity spaces, lower mobility entropy, and different temporal usage. The research highlights that mobility models trained predominantly on majority populations misrepresent elderly behavior, particularly in spatial metrics, leading to biased synthetic trajectory generation. Using both a first-order Markov chain and a fine-tuned large language model, the study compares models trained on the full population, young riders only, and elderly riders only. Results show that models trained specifically on elderly data produce more accurate representations, while higher-capability models do not necessarily improve subgroup fidelity when demographic data is limited. These findings emphasize the need for inclusive demographic representation in urban mobility modeling to avoid systematic biases affecting underrepresented groups.

item.title: Researchers introduce RosettaSim, a structured autoregressive model for long-term multi-agent traffic simulation achieving state-of-the-art results on Waymo Open Sim Agent Challenge [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed RosettaSim, a structured autoregressive model designed for long-term multi-agent traffic simulation, which achieves state-of-the-art results on the Waymo Open Sim Agent Challenge. The model leverages the architectural strengths and statistical priors of large-scale sequence models, such as Large Language Models, to effectively handle dynamic multi-agent interactions over extended periods. RosettaSim encodes scene topology, agent states, and spawning intents into a variable-length autoregressive stream, enabling both accurate short-term predictions and stable long-term simulation fidelity. To evaluate extended simulations where direct agent correspondence diminishes over time, the team introduced Retrieval-based Traffic Evaluation (RTE), a method that uses semantically similar real-world scenarios as reference points. Experiments demonstrate that RosettaSim outperforms existing approaches in both short- and long-term traffic simulation, with RTE showing a stronger correlation to standard metrics, indicating improved alignment with real-world traffic dynamics.

item.title: Researchers introduce PEC-CIR, a training-free multi-stage reasoning framework for zero-shot composed image retrieval that improves query construction and retrieval stability through planning, execution, and self-criticism [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed PEC-CIR, a training-free, multi-stage reasoning framework designed to improve zero-shot composed image retrieval. This approach enhances query construction and retrieval stability by breaking down the process into three stages: planning, execution, and self-criticism. Unlike existing single-pass methods that combine reference images and textual modifications into one description, PEC-CIR uses a Planner to extract constraints, an Executor to generate multiple candidate queries, and a Critic to evaluate these candidates for compliance, reducing semantic errors and improving retrieval accuracy. By structuring query construction as a staged inference process rather than a single-step output, PEC-CIR addresses challenges such as semantic distortions and attribute preservation conflicts that degrade retrieval precision. This framework operates within a frozen vision-language embedding space at inference time, enabling more robust and stable retrieval without additional training.

item.title: Researchers propose Agentic-Ideation framework with Oracle-Guided Data Synthesis to improve sample efficiency and quality of scientific ideation agents by over 10 times and 11.9% respectively [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Agentic-Ideation, a new framework designed to enhance scientific ideation agents by significantly improving sample efficiency and output quality. This approach combines an automated trajectory synthesis pipeline with a specialized agentic large language model (LLM) trained for scientific ideation, addressing limitations of previous methods that relied on rigid workflows and faced high data synthesis costs. The framework incorporates a comprehensive set of tools and employs an Oracle-Guided Data Synthesis strategy that uses reference ideas to guide multi-agent systems in generating more directed and efficient reasoning paths. The method trains the agent on synthesized trajectories with a masking strategy to focus on decision-making logic, avoiding interference from external feedback. Experimental results show that Agentic-Ideation outperforms state-of-the-art workflow-based baselines by 11.9% in overall quality and achieves over a tenfold increase in sample efficiency for high-quality data synthesis. This advancement offers a promising direction for more flexible and cost-effective automated scientific discovery processes.

item.title: Researchers propose Delta-JEPA, a reconstruction-free world model using latent difference action decoding to improve action-sensitive planning in visual continuous-control tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced Delta-JEPA, a novel reconstruction-free world model designed to enhance action-sensitive planning in visual continuous-control tasks.
