This model incorporates a Latent Difference Action Decoder (LDAD) that reconstructs executed actions from the latent displacement between consecutive observations, ensuring that latent representations remain sensitive to actions and avoid collapse into action-insensitive forms. Delta-JEPA relies solely on latent prediction and action reconstruction, bypassing traditional pixel reconstruction and distribution-matching methods. Tested across four visual continuous-control tasks, Delta-JEPA demonstrated improved planning performance compared to existing JEPA-based and representation-learning world models. The approach's displacement-based action decoding proved more effective than endpoint concatenation, and analyses confirmed clearer action-conditioned latent responses. These findings suggest that supervising latent differences offers a straightforward and effective strategy for developing collapse-resistant, action-sensitive world models.

item.title: Researchers present Embodied CAD, solver-grounded large language model agents for parametric B-Rep assembly modeling with iterative action selection and solver feedback, evaluated on multi-step industrial tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Embodied CAD, a system that integrates large language models with solver-grounded feedback to improve parametric boundary representation (B-Rep) assembly modeling in computer-aided design (CAD). Unlike traditional methods that generate complete scripts in one step, this approach iteratively selects actions from a hierarchical CAD skill library, executes them in a CAD backend, and uses solver feedback to refine planning and repair processes. This method ensures that every feature and assembly relation is validated by an exact geometric kernel, maintaining editability and precision. The framework combines action grammar constraints, deterministic parameter resolution, and solver-derived rewards to enhance learning and execution. Evaluations on complex mechanical and industrial assembly tasks demonstrate that solver-grounded planning successfully completes all benchmark workflows, while learned controllers achieve high executable rates, highlighting the gap between valid tool usage and precise long-term policy prediction. This advancement offers a promising direction for reliable and editable industrial CAD modeling driven by AI.

item.title: Researchers introduce modality switching between language and symbolic grids to improve spatial reasoning in large language models by up to 42% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method to enhance spatial reasoning in large language models (LLMs) by enabling them to switch between natural language and symbolic grid representations. This approach is based on the observation that human reasoning often involves multiple modalities, such as diagrams or grids, to better understand complex problems. The study introduces a switching metric that helps the model decide when to use language-based reasoning and when to rely on structured spatial representations, leading to performance improvements of up to 42% in reasoning tasks. The research focuses on grounding multi-hop textual-spatial stories into geometry-aware modalities like layouts or grids, comparing this to traditional natural language inference. By assessing trustworthiness and complexity signals, the model can determine the most effective modality for a given problem. This work represents a step toward more principled modality selection in LLM reasoning, highlighting the significant impact of modality choice on reasoning outcomes.

item.title: Researchers benchmark 14 large language models on floating-point error classification using InterFLOPBench with 1,130 test samples across six error categories, finding top models exceed 0.88 F1-score [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have evaluated the ability of 14 large language models (LLMs) to detect and classify floating-point errors in software code using a new benchmark called InterFLOPBench. This benchmark includes 1,130 test samples from 90 C kernels and covers six categories of floating-point errors: cancellation, comparison, division by zero, overflow, underflow, and NaN. The study treats error detection as a multi-label classification task and measures performance with the F1-score metric, finding that the latest models achieve overall F1-scores above 0.88. The evaluation revealed variation in model performance across different error types, with explicit errors like division by zero scoring higher (average F1-score of 0.85) compared to more subtle numerical issues such as underflow and cancellation, which had lower average scores around 0.61. Top-performing models include Qwen 3 32b, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Phi 4 Reasoning, DeepSeek R1T2, and gpt-oss variants, demonstrating strong capabilities in static floating-point error classification.

item.title: Researchers release HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, a French multi-hop question answering dataset with 1782 questions from parliamentary debates and newspapers of the French Third Republic (1870-1940) for historical research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, a French-language dataset designed for multi-hop question answering in historical research. The dataset contains 1,782 questions derived from parliamentary debates and newspapers of the French Third Republic (1870-1940), emphasizing complex reasoning such as cross-source synthesis and temporal analysis. Developed in collaboration with a historian, it aims to support evaluation of retrieval-augmented and large language model systems within domain-specific contexts. The creation of HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic involved careful selection and alignment of heterogeneous historical sources, question validation, and integration of metadata. While focused on French historical documents, the methodology used to build the corpus can be adapted to other languages and national archives. This resource bridges the gap between natural language processing benchmarks and the practical needs of historical scholarship by enabling realistic evaluation scenarios for multi-hop question answering.

item.title: CryoACE introduces an atom-centric framework for automated, accurate protein model building from cryo-EM density maps, enabling dynamic atomic-level conformations without pre-built static structures [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: CryoACE is a new automated framework designed to build accurate protein models directly from cryo-EM density maps, addressing challenges in maintaining physicochemical validity and handling conformational variability. It introduces an atom-centric approach that samples density features at atomic coordinates and iteratively refines structures, replacing traditional voxel-based methods for more efficient data fusion. Additionally, it employs a training-free guidance system using local resolution predictions to resolve dynamic ambiguities. Tested on a high-quality dataset, CryoACE outperforms existing methods on static structure benchmarks and uniquely reveals atomic-level dynamic conformations in complex real-world datasets without relying on pre-existing static models. This advancement offers a significant step forward in modeling both homogeneous and heterogeneous protein structures from cryo-EM data.

item.title: Survey of 78 joint OFDM-RIS optimization algorithms for 6G networks classifies methods from convex relaxation to foundation models and identifies six open challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A comprehensive survey reviews 78 studies on joint OFDM-RIS optimization for 6G networks, addressing challenges such as sum-rate maximization, energy efficiency, fairness, and peak-to-average power ratio constraints. The research categorizes existing methods into four paradigms: model-based convex relaxation, heuristic/metaheuristic search, deep reinforcement and unsupervised learning, and emerging approaches including foundation models and quantum optimization. The survey highlights that machine learning techniques achieve near-model-based spectral efficiency with significantly faster runtimes, and identifies a critical scaling advantage of neural network inference over iterative solvers. The study notes the absence of standardized benchmarks, making cross-comparison difficult, and presents a tutorial benchmark revealing runtime invariance in GPU-based neural network methods across different problem sizes. It also outlines six key open challenges, including the need for standardized benchmarking, real-world hardware constraints, optimization for complex channel conditions, multi-objective trade-offs, safety concerns with large language models in network control, and the limited gains from standalone heuristics. This work provides a roadmap for future research and practical deployment of joint OFDM-RIS optimization in 6G systems.

item.title: Researchers compare independent multi-agent reinforcement learning methods for decentralized smart charging of large electric vehicle fleets under dynamic pricing and grid constraints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have compared two independent multi-agent reinforcement learning methods-contextual combinatorial bandits and policy gradient algorithms-for decentralized smart charging of large electric vehicle fleets. Their study addresses challenges posed by increased peak demand and grid constraints due to EV integration, aiming to optimize charging schedules under dynamic electricity pricing and network limitations. The evaluation was conducted in a realistic simulation where autonomous agents make decisions based on local information such as price signals, battery state, and timing constraints. The research tested these approaches across different congestion levels and heterogeneous agent groups, using dynamic pricing derived from real photovoltaic energy production data. This work highlights the potential of decentralized coordination among electric vehicles to minimize user costs and prevent grid overloads while accommodating renewable energy variability.

item.title: Researchers introduce ReGRPO, a reflection-augmented policy optimization framework that improves tool-using vision-language agents by learning reflection-guided corrections, outperforming open-source baselines on GTA and GAIA tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed ReGRPO, a reflection-augmented policy optimization framework designed to enhance the performance of tool-using vision-language models (VLMs) in solving complex multimodal tasks. ReGRPO addresses limitations in existing methods by learning reflection-guided corrections, enabling agents to recover from tool failures more effectively. The approach involves collecting failure observations through near-miss actions and creating Reflection-of-Thought triplets that guide corrective actions, which are optimized jointly to improve task success. The framework was tested on GTA and GAIA benchmarks, where it consistently outperformed strong open-source baselines using the same backbone and tool suite. ReGRPO incorporates a reflection-cost term to minimize unnecessary reflection, balancing correction with efficiency. The researchers have made their code and reflection data publicly available, supporting further development in tool-augmented vision-language agents.

item.title: Researchers identify phase transition causing sudden world-model collapse in long-horizon language agents, revealing a measurable bottleneck in agent performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a phase transition in long-horizon language agents that leads to a sudden collapse of their implicit world models. This phenomenon occurs when small changes in parameters, such as state load or horizon length, push the agent past a critical boundary, causing a rapid degradation in world-state fidelity despite maintaining valid actions. The study, conducted on a deterministic task family with exact per-step gold state, reveals a phase diagram with distinct regions of stable performance, transition, and collapse, highlighting a measurable bottleneck in agent performance. The research involved a comprehensive grid search over various factors including state cardinality, dependency density, horizon, branching, observation mode, and mutation rate. Findings show that stronger models shift the critical boundary but do not eliminate the qualitative transition, indicating that world-model collapse is an inherent challenge for long-horizon agents. This insight advances understanding of the limitations in agent world modeling and may guide future improvements in their design and robustness.

item.title: Researchers investigate artificial swarm intelligence in large language models, finding up to 37% error reduction across GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 in estimation tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have explored whether large language models (LLMs) can replicate the collective accuracy of human swarm intelligence through artificial swarms. In a controlled study involving 960 prompts across three models-GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.5-they tested both intra-model sampling and inter-model aggregation on eight estimation tasks, finding error reductions of up to 37% in mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). The study also identified correlations between confidence interval widths and estimation errors, indicating that LLMs may have metacognitive awareness when evaluating uncertainty. The experiment demonstrated consistent improvements in accuracy through aggregation strategies within and across models, suggesting that artificial swarms of LLMs can enhance decision-making processes. These findings provide valuable insights for applying LLM swarms in organizational contexts, potentially overcoming limitations of human swarm intelligence related to cost, coordination, and scalability.

item.title: Xiaomi releases Xiaomi-GUI-0, a multimodal GUI agent trained and evaluated on real mobile devices achieving over 72% success on RealMobile and 78.9% on AndroidWorld benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Xiaomi has introduced Xiaomi-GUI-0, a multimodal graphical user interface (GUI) agent designed to operate in real mobile environments. Unlike previous GUI agents trained on simulated data, Xiaomi-GUI-0 is developed and evaluated using real devices, achieving success rates of 72.0% on the RealMobile benchmark and 78.9% on AndroidWorld. This approach addresses the gap between benchmark performance and real-world usability by incorporating physical devices into its training and evaluation loop, enhancing execution stability and abnormal-state recognition. The agent is built on a hybrid infrastructure that prioritizes real-device execution supported by sandboxes, enabling data collection and training that closely mirror actual deployment conditions. Its training involves diverse data sources covering common tasks, long-tail intents, and capabilities like reflection and memory, alongside an error-driven data flywheel that refines the model through corrected actions and recovery demonstrations. Xiaomi-GUI-0 undergoes a progressive training pipeline including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning stages to improve its performance in complex, real-world mobile interactions.

item.title: Researchers propose BP-TTA method combining balanced sampling and prototype-guided adaptation to address class imbalance and continual domain shifts in dynamic test-time scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have introduced BP-TTA, a new method for Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) that addresses both class imbalance and continual domain shifts in dynamic test-time scenarios. BP-TTA combines balanced batch sampling with prototype-guided adaptation to improve model performance when adapting to unlabeled test data streams that exhibit changing distributions and uneven class representation. The method constructs balanced adaptation batches by mixing current samples with high-confidence historical data, reducing bias toward dominant classes and stabilizing online updates. It also maintains evolving class prototypes during inference, using prototype similarity to guide adaptation and enhance the reliability of pseudo-labels. Experiments show that BP-TTA outperforms existing TTA approaches in handling dynamic, real-world test-time streaming conditions.

item.title: Researchers introduce a budgeted environment probing method for calibrating world models in long-horizon language agents to reduce terminal errors during task planning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a budgeted environment probing method called \method to improve the calibration of world models used by long-horizon language agents during task planning. This approach allows agents to query the environment selectively about specific belief fields before taking actions, helping to correct model drift and reduce errors that could lead to task failures. By treating environment interaction as a limited resource for calibration rather than just task progression, the method enhances the agent's decision-making accuracy over extended sequences of actions. The study distinguishes between different types of beliefs within the agent's model, such as procedural beliefs related to tool dependencies and spatial beliefs concerning object locations and relationships. Targeted environment probes can effectively repair procedural beliefs, while spatial beliefs require structural cues due to challenges like off-screen changes. Controlled experiments demonstrate that incorporating mid-planning environment feedback following the task's structure significantly lowers terminal errors in the world model, highlighting the value of strategic probing in complex task environments.
